title.zh: 卷九十九 列傳第六十九 桓玄 卞範之 殷仲文
title.en: Volume 99 Biographies 69: Huan Xuan; Bian Fanzhi; Duan Zhongwen
title.raw: 卷九十九 列傳第六十九 桓玄 卞範之 殷仲文 Volume 99 Biographies 69: Huan Xuan; Bian Fanzhi; Duan Zhongwen

sentences.zh: 桓玄，字敬道，一名靈寶，大司馬溫之孽子也。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan, courtesy name Jingdao, also named Lingbao, was the illegitimate son of Grand Marshal Huan Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan—courtesy name Jingdao, also known as Lingbao—was the illegitimate son of Grand Marshal Huan Wen.

sentences.zh: 其母馬氏嘗與同輩夜坐，於月下見流星墜銅盆水中，忽如二寸火珠，冏然明淨，競以瓢接取，馬氏得而吞之，若有感，遂有娠。

translations.literal: His mother, the Lady Ma, once sat with her peers at night; under the moon she saw a shooting star fall into the water of a bronze basin; suddenly it was like a two-inch ball of fire, bright and limpid; they vied to catch it with ladles; Lady Ma caught it and swallowed it; she seemed to respond to something, and thereafter became pregnant.
translations.idiomatic: Once at night his mother, Lady Ma, sat among companions and watched a shooting star fall into a bronze basin of water in the moonlight; it looked suddenly like a bead of flame two inches across, dazzlingly bright and clear. They scrambled to scoop it up with ladles; Lady Ma caught it and swallowed it, felt something stir within her, and conceived.

sentences.zh: 及生玄，有光照室，占者奇之，故小名靈寶。

translations.literal: When Xuan was born, there was light which illuminated the chamber; the diviners deemed it extraordinary; hence his childhood name Lingbao.
translations.idiomatic: At his birth light filled the room; diviners pronounced it a marvel, which is why his infant name was Lingbao.

sentences.zh: 妳媼每抱詣溫，輒易人而後至，雲其重兼常兒，溫甚愛異之。

translations.literal: The nurse, whenever she carried him to see Wen, always switched carriers before arriving, saying that his weight was twice that of an ordinary child; Wen greatly cherished him as something extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever his nurse brought him to Huan Wen, she would switch carriers before they arrived, claiming the boy weighed twice what a normal infant did; Wen adored him all the more as something remarkable.

sentences.zh: 臨終，命以為嗣，襲爵南郡公。

translations.literal: At his deathbed, [Wen] ordered that [Xuan] succeed him; [Xuan] inherited the noble rank of Duke of Nanjun.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Wen designated him heir, and he succeeded to the ducal title of Nanjun.

sentences.zh: 年七歲，溫服終，府州文武辭其叔父沖，沖撫玄頭曰：「此汝家之故吏也。

translations.literal: At age seven, when Wen's mourning period ended, the civil and military officers of the headquarters took leave of his uncle Chong; Chong stroked Xuan's head and said: "These are your family's former subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: When he was seven and Wen's mourning had ended, the civil and military officers of headquarters paid their respects to his uncle Huan Chong; Chong stroked Xuan's head and said, "They are the old retainers of your house.

sentences.zh: 」玄因涕淚覆面，眾並異之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xuan wept until tears covered his face; all marvelled at him.
translations.idiomatic: At that Xuan wept until tears streamed down his face; everyone was struck by him.

sentences.zh: 及長，形貌瑰奇，風神疏朗，博綜藝術，善屬文。

translations.literal: When grown, his appearance was striking and curious; his bearing open and bright; he broadly mastered arts and skills; he excelled at composing texts.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he cut an extraordinary figure, carried himself with ease and clarity, mastered many arts, and wrote well.

sentences.zh: 常負其才地，以雄豪自處，眾咸憚之，朝廷亦疑而未用。

translations.literal: He constantly relied on his talent and pedigree, comporting himself as a formidable champion; all feared him; the court also suspected him and did not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: He leaned on his gifts and family stature and acted the fearless hero; officials dreaded him, and the court hesitated to give him real responsibility.

sentences.zh: 年二十三，始拜太子洗馬，時議謂溫有不臣之跡，故折玄兄弟而為素官。

translations.literal: At twenty-three he first received appointment as Junior Groom of the Heir Apparent; opinion at the time held that Wen had shown signs of disloyalty; hence Xuan and his brothers were checked and given sinecure offices.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-three he was appointed groom-in-waiting to the heir apparent; court gossip held that Wen had revealed ambitions beyond his station, so Xuan and his brothers were sidelined into ornamental posts.

sentences.zh: 太元末，出補義興太守，鬱鬱不得志。

translations.literal: Toward the end of the Taiyuan era he was sent out as prefect of Yixing; depressed and unable to fulfill his ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Taiyuan period he was posted prefect of Yixing, where he brooded, thwarted in his ambitions.

sentences.zh: 嘗登高望震澤，歎曰：「父為九州伯，兒為五湖長！

translations.literal: He once climbed high to gaze at Lake Zhen and sighed: "My father was lord of the Nine Provinces; his son is chief of the Five Lakes!
translations.idiomatic: Once he climbed a height to look out over Lake Zhen and cried, "My father stood astride the realm; I am nothing but steward of the lakes!

sentences.zh: 」棄官歸國。

translations.literal: "He resigned office and returned to his domain.
translations.idiomatic: He threw down his office and went home to his fief.

sentences.zh: 自以元勳之門而負謗於世，乃上疏曰：

translations.literal: Considering himself of a merit lineage yet bearing slander in the world, he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Believing his house had earned great merit yet was maligned in public opinion, he presented a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞周公大聖而四國流言，樂毅王佐而被謗騎劫，《巷伯》有豺獸之慨，蘇公興飄風之刺，惡直醜正，何代無之！

translations.literal: "I have heard that the Duke of Zhou was the greatest of sages yet the four states spread rumors; Le Yi was a king's helper yet was slandered by Qi Jie; the "Lane Keeper" lamented jackal-beasts; Duke Su raised the "Whirling Wind" satire—evil hates the straight and mocks the upright; which generation has lacked them!
translations.idiomatic: "I have heard how even the Duke of Zhou, sage among sages, faced rumor across the states; how Le Yi, pillar of the throne, was torn down by slander; how the ode "Lane Keeper" rails at jackals, how "Whirling Wind" flays hypocrisy—the crooked always despise the upright: what age has ever been free of it?

sentences.zh: 先臣蒙國殊遇，姻婭皇極，常欲以身報德，投袂乘機，西平巴蜀，北清伊洛，使竊號之寇系頸北闕，園陵修復，大恥載雪，飲馬灞滻懸旌趙魏，勤王之師，功非一捷。

translations.literal: "My late father received the state's extraordinary favor and marriage ties to the imperial house; he always wished to repay its kindness with his person, to seize the moment, to pacify Ba–Shu in the west and clear the Yi and Luo in the north, to make the bandits who had seized the throne bind their necks at the northern gate, to restore the imperial tombs, to wash away the great shame at one stroke, to water horses at Ba and Chan and plant banners in Zhao and Wei—armies aiding the king do not succeed by a single stroke.
translations.idiomatic: "My late father enjoyed singular honors from the court and kinship with the throne; he burned to repay that debt with his life—strike west to settle Ba and Shu, sweep north to clear the Yi and Luo, drag pretenders in shackles to the capital gates, repair the imperial tombs, expunge national shame in one campaign, water horses along Ba and Chan and raise standards through Zhao and Wei. Forces raised for the king win no single decisive clash alone.

sentences.zh: 太和之末，皇基有潛移之懼，遂乃奉順天人，翼登聖朝，明離既朗，四凶兼澄。

translations.literal: "At the end of the Taihe reign the dynastic foundation feared a stealthy shift; therefore following Heaven and man he aided the ascent of the sacred court; once the bright sun shone, the Four Fiends were all cleared.
translations.idiomatic: "When at the close of Taihe the dynasty seemed about to slip from its foundations, he obeyed Heaven and the human tide and helped elevate this sacred court; once legitimate radiance returned, every malignant faction was swept away.

sentences.zh: 向使此功不建，此事不成，宗廟之事豈可孰念！

translations.literal: "Had this achievement not been accomplished and this deed not finished, how could matters of the ancestral temples have been sustained!
translations.idiomatic: "Had that work not been done, how could the imperial ancestral cult even have been spoken of?

sentences.zh: 昔太甲雖迷，商祚無憂；

translations.literal: "Of old Taijia though astray, the Shang sacrifice knew no worry;
translations.idiomatic: "Ancient Taijia wandered from duty, yet Yin sacrifices continued untroubled;

sentences.zh: 昌邑雖昏，弊無三孽。

translations.literal: "the Prince of Changyi though dim, his harm did not match three calamities.
translations.idiomatic: "the Prince of Changyi was dull, yet his misrule never matched threefold disaster.

sentences.zh: 因茲而言，晉室之機危于殷漢，先臣之功高於伊霍矣。

translations.literal: "From this it follows that the house of Jin stood in greater peril than Yin or Han, and my late father's merit towered above Yi Yin and Huo Guang.
translations.idiomatic: "By that measure the Jin throne faced sharper peril than Yin or Han ever knew, while my father's restoration towered above the deeds of Yi Yin and Huo Guang.

sentences.zh: 而負重既往，蒙謗清時，聖世明王黜陟之道，不聞廢忽顯明之功，探射冥冥之心，啟嫌謗之塗，開邪枉之路者也。

translations.literal: "Yet bearing blame once incurred, he suffered slander in a clear age—the way sage kings promote and demote ought not mean casting aside manifest merit, probing hearts in the dark, opening roads of suspicion and slander and twisted wrong.
translations.idiomatic: "Yet once maligned, he stood accused in an enlightened reign—true kings reward and punish fairly; they do not bury shining deeds, probe unknowable motives, invite reckless rumor, or widen avenues of intrigue.

sentences.zh: 先臣勤王艱難之勞，匡復克平之勳，朝廷若其遺之，臣亦不復計也。

translations.literal: "As for my late father's hardships in aiding the king and his feats of restoration and pacification—if the court casts them aside, I shall pursue the matter no further.
translations.idiomatic: "If the court chooses to forget my father's sacrifices to rescue the throne and his victories of restoration, I will say no more.

sentences.zh: 至於先帝龍飛九五，陛下之所以繼明南面，請問談者，誰之由邪？

translations.literal: "When it comes to the late emperor's ascending the throne and why Your Majesty faces south in succession—ask those who speak: through whom did it come?
translations.idiomatic: "But when you ask who placed the late emperor on the throne—who allowed Your Majesty to face south and inherit the mandate—the answer is plain.

sentences.zh: 誰之德邪？

translations.literal: "Through whose virtue?
translations.idiomatic: "Through whose merit?

sentences.zh: 豈惟晉室永安，祖宗血食，于陛下一門，實奇功也。

translations.literal: "It is not only that the house of Jin would enjoy lasting peace and the ancestors receive blood offerings—for Your Majesty's single lineage it was truly a singular achievement.
translations.idiomatic: "This secured more than lasting peace for Jin and continued offerings to the imperial shrines—it delivered Your Majesty's line an extraordinary debt.

sentences.zh: 自頃權門日盛，醜政實繁，咸稱述時旨，互相扇附，以臣之兄弟皆晉之罪人，臣等復何理可以苟存聖世？

translations.literal: "Recently powerful houses strengthen daily; ugly government proliferates; all echo this hour's tone and fan each other on, claiming my brothers are criminals of Jin—in what principle may we shamefully linger in this sacred age?
translations.idiomatic: "Today magnates swell their influence while misrule grows worse; each mouths current slogans and eggs the others on, branding my brothers Jin's traitors—under what right could we linger disgracefully at court?

sentences.zh: 何顏可以屍饗封祿？

translations.literal: "In what face may we receive salary and noble rank?
translations.idiomatic: "How could we still collect stipends and titles without shame?

sentences.zh: 若陛下忘先臣大造之功，信貝錦萋菲之說，臣等自當奉還三封，受戮市朝，然後下從先臣，歸先帝于玄宮耳。

translations.literal: "If Your Majesty forgets my late father's foundational merit and trusts twisted tongues like patterned shells and luxuriant lies, we shall ourselves return the three fiefs and accept execution in the marketplace, then follow our late father below and join the late emperor in the dark palace.
translations.idiomatic: "Should Your Majesty discard my father's foundational deeds and credit twisted hearsay, we will surrender our three noble jurisdictions and face the executioner's blade in the marketplace, then join our father among the dead below.

sentences.zh: 若陛下述遵先旨，追錄舊勳，竊望少垂愷悌覆蓋之恩。

translations.literal: "If Your Majesty follows prior intent and records old merit, I humbly hope you will show a little gentle grace that shelters us.
translations.idiomatic: "If instead Your Majesty honors earlier pledges and restores past honors, I pray only for a modest measure of kindly indulgence.

sentences.zh: 疏寢不報。

translations.literal: The memorial slept without reply.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial drew no answer.

sentences.zh: 玄在荊楚積年，優遊無事，荊州刺史殷仲堪甚敬憚之。

translations.literal: Xuan dwelt in Jing–Chu for many years, idle and at ease; Yin Zhongkan, Inspector of Jingzhou, deeply respected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan spent years idle in Jing and Chu; Yin Zhongkan, who governed Jingzhou, respected him greatly—and feared him.

sentences.zh: 及中書令王國寶用事，謀削弱方鎮，內外騷動，知王恭有憂國之言，玄潛有意于功業，乃說仲堪曰：「國寶與君諸人素已為對，唯患相弊之不速耳。

translations.literal: When Palace Writer Wang Guobao wielded power and plotted to weaken the regional commands, turmoil stirred inside and out; knowing Wang Gong harbored concern for the state, Xuan secretly aspired to merit and persuaded Zhongkan: "Guobao and you gentlemen have long been at odds; he only worries that mutual harm does not come quickly enough.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wang Guobao dominated the Secretariat and schemed to clip provincial power, capital and regions alike seethed; seeing Wang Gong poised to move for the dynasty's sake, Xuan secretly sought glory and urged Zhongkan: "Guobao and your circle have long been enemies—he only laments you have not destroyed each other sooner.

sentences.zh: 今既執權要，與王緒相為表裏，其所回易，罔不如志。

translations.literal: "Now that he holds power, he and Wang Xu back each other; whatever he turns or replaces follows his desire.
translations.idiomatic: "Now he grips authority and works hand in glove with Wang Xu; every reshuffle answers his whim.

sentences.zh: 孝伯居元舅之地，正情為朝野所重，必未便動之，唯當以君為事首。

translations.literal: "Xiaobo occupies the station of chief maternal uncle; his integrity carries weight at court and in the countryside—[Guobao] will surely not move him lightly; he will only take you as the first target.
translations.idiomatic: "Wang Gong—the emperor's maternal uncle—commands moral prestige throughout court and countryside; Guobao will hardly strike him first—you will be his opening blow.

sentences.zh: 君為先帝所拔，超居方任，人情未以為允，咸謂君雖有思致，非方伯人。

translations.literal: "You were promoted by the late emperor beyond ordinary station to regional duty; popular feeling does not yet deem it fitting—all say that though you have ideas, you are not material for a regional lord.
translations.idiomatic: "You owe your frontier command to the late emperor's sudden favor; people still doubt you truly belong in such a post—they concede your wit yet insist you lack the backbone of a governor.

sentences.zh: 若發詔征君為中書令，用殷顗為荊州，君何以處之？

translations.literal: "If an edict summons you as Palace Writer and appoints Yin Yi to Jingzhou, how will you handle it?
translations.idiomatic: "What will you do if an edict recalls you to be Palace Writer and gives Jingzhou to Yin Yi?

sentences.zh: 」仲堪曰：「憂之久矣，君謂計將安出？

translations.literal: Zhongkan said: "I have long worried; what plan do you propose?
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan replied, "That fear has gnawed at me—what course do you advise?

sentences.zh: 」玄曰：「國寶奸凶，天下所知，孝伯疾惡之情每至而當，今日之會，以理推之，必當過人。

translations.literal: "Xuan said: "Guobao is treacherous and wicked—the world knows it; Xiaobo's hatred of evil always meets the mark; by reason this meeting must surpass others.
translations.idiomatic: "Xuan answered, "Guobao's villainy is notorious; Wang Gong hates wickedness to the bone—by rights his outrage must outstrip ours.

sentences.zh: 君若密遣一人，信說王恭，宜興晉陽之師，以內匡朝廷，己當悉荊楚之眾順流而下，推王為盟主，僕等亦皆投袂，當此無不回應。

translations.literal: "If you secretly dispatch someone to tell Wang Gong he should raise the army of Jinyang to rectify the court within, while you bring all the hosts of Jing–Chu downstream and support Wang as covenant chief—we too will all flap our sleeves to join; at such a moment none will fail to answer.
translations.idiomatic: "Send a confidential envoy urging Wang Gong to raise troops like those at Jinyang and sweep the capital clean while you march every man Jing and Chu can spare downstream and install Wang as league chief—we will all rally—and none will refuse.

sentences.zh: 此事既行，桓文之舉也。

translations.literal: "When this deed is done, it will be an act worthy of Dukes Huan and Wen.
translations.idiomatic: "Victory would crown deeds worthy of the great hegemons Huan and Wen.

sentences.zh: 」仲堪持疑未決。

translations.literal: Zhongkan hesitated and did not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan wavered and could not commit.

sentences.zh: 俄而王恭信至，招仲堪及玄匡正朝廷。

translations.literal: Soon Wang Gong's letter arrived, summoning Zhongkan and Xuan to set the court right.
translations.idiomatic: Presently Wang Gong's summons arrived, calling Zhongkan and Xuan to restore imperial authority.

sentences.zh: 國寶既死，於是兵罷。

translations.literal: After Guobao died, the armies stood down.
translations.idiomatic: Once Guobao fell, the armies dispersed.

sentences.zh: 玄乃求為廣州，會稽王道子亦憚之，不欲使在荊楚，故順其意。

translations.literal: Xuan then requested Guangzhou; Prince of Kuaiji Sima Daozi also feared him and did not wish him to remain in Jing–Chu, so he indulged that wish.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan applied for Guangzhou; Prince Daozi of Kuaiji likewise dreaded keeping him in Jing-Chu and indulged the request.

sentences.zh: 隆安初，詔以玄督交廣二州、建威將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史、假節，玄受命不行。

translations.literal: At the start of Long'an, an edict named Xuan to supervise Jiao and Guang two prefectures, General Who Builds Might, Central Colonel Who Pacifies the Yue, Prefect of Guangzhou, with credential authority—Xuan accepted the order but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Long'an an edict named him governor of Jiao and Guang, General Who Inspires Awe, Interior Colonel for Pacifying the Yue, prefect of Guangzhou, with plenary authority—Xuan took the appointment yet refused to travel south.

sentences.zh: 其年，王恭又與庾楷起兵討江州刺史王愉及譙王尚之兄弟。

translations.literal: That year Wang Gong again, with Yu Kai, raised troops to attack Prefect of Jiangzhou Wang Yu and Prince of Qiao Wang Shangzhi and his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Wang Gong joined Yu Kai in arms against Jiangzhou prefect Wang Yu and Prince Shangzhi of Qiao with his brothers.

sentences.zh: 玄、仲堪謂恭事必克捷，一時回應。

translations.literal: Xuan and Zhongkan deemed Gong's affair sure to succeed and answered at once.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan and Zhongkan assumed Gong would prevail and pledged immediate support.

sentences.zh: 仲堪給玄五千人，與楊佺期俱為前鋒。

translations.literal: Zhongkan supplied Xuan with five thousand men; together with Yang Quanqi he served as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan gave Xuan five thousand troops; together with Yang Quanqi they formed the spearhead.

sentences.zh: 軍至湓口，王愉奔於臨川，玄遣偏將軍追獲之。

translations.literal: When the army reached Penkou, Wang Yu fled to Linchuan; Xuan sent a deputy general in pursuit and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: When the force reached Penkou, Wang Yu bolted for Linchuan; Xuan detached a column that ran him down and took him captive.

sentences.zh: 玄、佺期至石頭，仲堪至蕪湖。

translations.literal: Xuan and Quanqi reached Stone Wall; Zhongkan reached Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan and Quanqi advanced on Jiankang's Stone bastion while Zhongkan closed on Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 恭將劉牢之背恭歸順。

translations.literal: Gong's general Liu Laozhi turned against Gong and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong's commander Liu Laozhi switched sides and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 恭既死，庾楷戰敗，奔于玄軍。

translations.literal: With Gong dead, Yu Kai was defeated in battle and fled to Xuan's army.
translations.idiomatic: Once Gong died, Yu Kai lost in the field and fled into Xuan's camp.

sentences.zh: 既而詔以玄為江州，仲堪等仲皆被換易，乃各回舟西還，屯于尋陽，共相結約，推玄為盟主。

translations.literal: Presently an edict assigned Xuan to Jiangzhou; Zhongkan and the others were all rotated out—therefore each turned ships west, encamped at Xunyang, jointly bound themselves, and made Xuan covenant chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict handed Jiangzhou to Xuan and reshuffled the others; each fleet sailed back west to Xunyang, swore a pact, and elected Xuan league chief.

sentences.zh: 玄始得志，乃連名上疏申理王恭，求誅尚之、牢之等。

translations.literal: Xuan had his wish and jointly submitted a memorial arguing Wang Gong's case, requesting execution of Shangzhi, Laozhi, and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Flush with success, they jointly memorialized to vindicate Wang Gong and demand death for Shangzhi, Laozhi, and company.

sentences.zh: 朝廷深憚之，乃免桓脩、復仲堪以相和解。

translations.literal: The court feared them deeply; it dismissed Huan Xiu and restored Zhongkan to reconcile.
translations.idiomatic: The court quailed and placated them by removing Huan Xiu from office and reinstating Zhongkan.

sentences.zh: 初，玄在荊州豪縱，士庶憚之，甚於州牧。

translations.literal: At first Xuan had run riot in Jingzhou; gentry and commoners feared him more than the provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xuan had bullied Jingzhou until scholars and commoners feared him more than their nominal governor.

sentences.zh: 仲堪親黨勸殺之，仲堪不聽。

translations.literal: Zhongkan's close associates urged killing him; Zhongkan would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan's inner circle begged to kill Xuan; Zhongkan refused.

sentences.zh: 及還尋陽，資其聲地，故推為盟主，玄逾自矜重。

translations.literal: When they returned to Xunyang, relying on his reputation and standing they pushed him as covenant chief; Xuan grew all the more arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Back at Xunyang they leaned on his fame and status to make him league chief, and Xuan grew insufferably proud.

sentences.zh: 佺期為人驕悍，常自謂承藉華胄，江表莫比，而玄每以寒士裁之，佺期甚憾，即欲於壇所襲玄，仲堪惡佺期兄弟虓勇，恐克玄之後復為己害，苦禁之。

translations.literal: Quanqi was by nature fierce and headstrong; he always claimed noble pedigree—none south of the Yangzi could compare—yet Xuan constantly treated him as a humble scholar; Quanqi deeply resented it and wished to ambush Xuan at the alliance altar; Zhongkan loathed the Quanqi brothers' tiger-like courage and feared that after defeating Xuan they would harm him too; he sternly forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: Quanqi was proud and violent, insisting no southern lineage surpassed his own, yet Xuan dismissed him as minor gentry; Quanqi nursed a bitter grudge and wanted to strike Xuan at the oath site. Zhongkan detested the brothers' ferocity and worried that after crushing Xuan they would turn on him, so he forbade any move.

sentences.zh: 於是各奉詔還鎮。

translations.literal: Thereupon each obeyed the edict and returned to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Each man then obeyed the recall and returned to his command.

sentences.zh: 玄亦知佺期有異謀，潛有吞併之計，於是屯于夏口。

translations.literal: Xuan also knew Quanqi harbored other designs and secretly planned to swallow him; he therefore encamped at Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan knew Quanqi nursed separate ambitions and quietly plotted to absorb him, so he camped at Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 隆安中，詔加玄都督荊州四郡，以兄偉為輔國將軍、南蠻校尉。

translations.literal: In Long'an an edict added Xuan as supervisor of four Jingzhou commanderies and appointed his elder brother Wei General Who Assists the State and Colonel of Southern Man.
translations.idiomatic: During Long'an an edict enlarged Xuan's brief to four Jingzhou counties and named his elder brother Huan Wei General Who Supports the State and Colonel of the Southern Man.

sentences.zh: 仲堪慮玄跋扈，遂與佺期結婚為援。

translations.literal: Zhongkan feared Xuan's domineering ways and therefore allied by marriage with Quanqi for support.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan dreaded Xuan's high-handedness and sealed the bond by marrying into Quanqi's family.

sentences.zh: 初，玄既與仲堪、佺期有隙，恆臣掩襲，求廣其所統。

translations.literal: At first, once Xuan had fallen out with Zhongkan and Quanqi, he secretly harbored plans of surprise attack and sought to expand what he commanded.
translations.idiomatic: Once relations with Zhongkan and Quanqi soured, Xuan quietly plotted raids and pushed to widen his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 朝廷亦欲成其釁隙，故分佺斯所督四郡與玄，佺期甚忿懼。

translations.literal: The court also wished to deepen their rift, so it divided the four commanderies Quanqi supervised and gave them to Xuan; Quanqi was furious and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The court likewise hoped to widen the breach and carved four counties from Quanqi's supervision for Xuan; Quanqi raged and trembled.

sentences.zh: 會姚興侵洛陽，佺期乃建牙，聲雲援洛，密欲與仲堪共襲玄。

translations.literal: When Yao Xing invaded Luoyang, Quanqi raised his banner, declaring publicly that he would aid Luoyang but secretly intending with Zhongkan to strike Xuan together.
translations.idiomatic: When Later Qin's Yao Xing pressed Luoyang, Quanqi unfurled banners claiming relief for the capital while secretly planning with Zhongkan to ambush Xuan.

sentences.zh: 仲堪雖外結佺期而疑其心，距而不許，猶慮弗能禁，復遣從弟遹屯于北境以遏佺期。

translations.literal: Zhongkan though outwardly allied with Quanqi doubted his intent, refused, and still feared he could not restrain him—he again sent his cousin You to encamp on the northern border to block Quanqi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan outwardly sided with Quanqi yet distrusted him, declined joint action, and still doubted he could hold Quanqi in check—so he stationed his cousin Yin You on the northern frontier to block him.

sentences.zh: 佺期既不能獨舉，且不測仲堪本意，遂息甲。

translations.literal: Quanqi could not act alone and could not fathom Zhongkan's true intent, so he stood his armor down.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to strike alone and unsure of Zhongkan's mind, Quanqi stood down.

sentences.zh: 南蠻校尉楊廣，佺期之兄也，欲距桓偉，仲堪不聽，乃出廣為宜都、建平二郡太守，加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: Colonel of Southern Man Yang Guang was Quanqi's elder brother; wishing to resist Huan Wei, Zhongkan would not allow it—instead he sent Guang out as prefect of Yidu and Jianping two commanderies, with added title General Who Subdues the Enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Man colonel Yang Guang, Quanqi's elder brother, wanted to fight Huan Wei, but Zhongkan refused; instead he posted Guang as prefect over Yidu and Jianping with the added title General Who Subdues the Foe.

sentences.zh: 佺期弟孜敬先為江夏相，玄以兵襲而召之。

translations.literal: Quanqi's younger brother Zijing had first been chief of Jiangxia; Xuan attacked by force and summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Quanqi's younger brother Yang Zijing had been magistrate of Jiangxia until Xuan struck, seized the district, and summoned him in.

sentences.zh: 既至，以為諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, Xuan made him consultant aide.
translations.idiomatic: After he arrived Xuan named him advisory aide.

sentences.zh: 玄於是興軍西征，亦聲雲救洛，與仲堪書，說佺期受國恩而棄山陵，宜共罪之。

translations.literal: Xuan thereupon raised an army for a western expedition, again declaring he would rescue Luoyang, and wrote Zhongkan accusing Quanqi of receiving the state's grace yet abandoning the tombs—they should jointly condemn him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan then mobilized a western relief army—again claiming rescue for Luoyang—and wrote Zhongkan charging Quanqi with betraying imperial grace by neglecting the royal tombs, urging joint condemnation.

sentences.zh: 今親率戎旅，逕造金墉，使仲堪收楊廣，如其不爾，無以相信。

translations.literal: "Now I lead the hosts in person straight to Jinyong; order Zhongkan to seize Yang Guang; if not, there is no basis for trust.
translations.idiomatic: "I now march in person on Jinyong; Zhongkan must arrest Yang Guang—otherwise no pact holds.

sentences.zh: 仲堪本計欲兩全之，既得玄書，知不能禁，乃曰：「君自沔而行，不得一人入江也。

translations.literal: Zhongkan's original plan was to preserve both; once he received Xuan's letter he knew he could not restrain him and said: "If you march from the Mian on your own, not a single man will enter the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan had hoped to keep both sides alive; Xuan's ultimatum showed restraint was futile, and he answered, "March down the Han if you wish—not one soldier crosses the Great River.

sentences.zh: 」玄乃止。

translations.literal: "Xuan then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan halted.

sentences.zh: 後荊州大水，仲堪振恤饑者，倉廩空竭。

translations.literal: Later Jingzhou suffered great flooding; Zhongkan relieved the hungry until granaries were empty.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward catastrophic floods struck Jingzhou; Zhongkan fed the starving until his granaries ran dry.

sentences.zh: 玄乘其虛而伐之，先遣軍襲巴陵。

translations.literal: Xuan exploited the weakness to attack; he first sent troops to raid Baling.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan seized the opening and struck, first sending columns against Baling.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史郭銓當之所鎮，路經夏口，玄聲雲朝廷遣銓為己前鋒，乃授以江夏之眾，使督諸軍並進，密報兄偉令為內應。

translations.literal: Inspector of Liangzhou Guo Quan was posted at his commandery; his route passed Xiakou; Xuan declared the court had sent Quan as his vanguard, assigned him the hosts of Jiangxia, had him oversee all columns advancing together, and secretly messaged his brother Wei to act as inner collaborator.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhou inspector Guo Quan's route to his post ran through Xiakou; Xuan announced the court had assigned Guo as his van, handed him Jiangxia's troops to coordinate every advance, and secretly told his brother Huan Wei to rise inside as fifth column.

sentences.zh: 偉遑遽不知所為，乃自齎疏示仲堪。

translations.literal: Wei in panic did not know what to do; he personally carried his memorial to show Zhongkan.
translations.idiomatic: Wei panicked; clutching his memorial he fled to Zhongkan.

sentences.zh: 仲堪執偉為質，令與玄書，辭甚苦至。

translations.literal: Zhongkan seized Wei as hostage and ordered him to write to Xuan in terms utterly bitter and urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan seized Wei as hostage and forced him to pen an anguished appeal to Xuan.

sentences.zh: 玄曰：「仲堪為人不得專決，常懷成敗之計，為兒子作慮，我兄必無憂矣。」

translations.literal: Xuan said: "Zhongkan cannot decide on his own; he always harbors calculations of success and failure and schemes for his sons—my brother is surely in no danger.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan scoffed, "Zhongkan cannot commit; he forever weighs odds for his sons—my brother faces no real peril.

sentences.zh: 玄既至巴陵，仲堪遣眾距之，為玄所敗。

translations.literal: Once Xuan reached Baling, Zhongkan sent troops to resist him and was defeated by Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan reached Baling, Zhongkan's defenders broke before him.

sentences.zh: 玄進至楊口，又敗仲堪弟子道護，乘勝至零口，去江陵二十里，仲堪遣軍數道距之。

translations.literal: Xuan advanced to Yangkou, again defeated Zhongkan's nephew Dao Hu, and pressed his victory to Lingkou, twenty li from Jiangling; Zhongkan sent troops along several routes to block him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan pressed to Yangkou, routed Zhongkan's nephew Yin Dao Hu, and drove within twenty li of Jiangling at Lingkou; Zhongkan threw multiple blocking lines against him.

sentences.zh: 佺期自襄陽來赴，與兄廣共擊玄，玄懼其銳，乃退軍馬頭。

translations.literal: Quanqi came from Xiangyang to aid him; together with his brother Guang he attacked Xuan; Xuan feared their sharpness and withdrew to Matou.
translations.idiomatic: Quanqi marched from Xiangyang with his brother Guang to strike Xuan; Xuan gave ground to their momentum and pulled back to Matou.

sentences.zh: 佺期等方復追玄苦戰，佺期敗，走還襄陽，仲堪出奔酂城，玄遣將軍馮該躡佺期，獲之。

translations.literal: Quanqi and the others again pursued Xuan and fought bitterly; Quanqi was defeated and fled back to Xiangyang; Zhongkan fled out to Zeng city; Xuan sent general Feng Gai to trail Quanqi and capture him.
translations.idiomatic: They renewed the pursuit and fought savagely; Quanqi broke and fled toward Xiangyang while Zhongkan bolted for Zengcheng; Xuan ordered Feng Gai to run Quanqi down and take him.

sentences.zh: 廣為人所縛，送玄，並殺之。

translations.literal: Guang was bound by others and sent to Xuan; both were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Others bound Guang and delivered him to Xuan; both brothers died.

sentences.zh: 仲堪聞佺期死，乃將數百人奔姚興，至冠軍城，為該所得，玄令害之。

translations.literal: When Zhongkan heard Quanqi was dead, he led several hundred men fleeing toward Yao Xing; reaching Champion city, he was taken by Feng Gai; Xuan ordered him killed.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Quanqi had fallen, Zhongkan fled toward Later Qin with a few hundred riders but Feng Gai seized him at Champion; Xuan had him executed.

sentences.zh: 於是遂平荊雍，乃表求領江、荊二州。

translations.literal: Thereupon he pacified Jing and Yong; he submitted a memorial requesting to head Jiang and Jing two prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: With Jing and Yong subdued, he memorialized to take both Jiang and Jing provinces himself.

sentences.zh: 詔以玄都督荊司雍秦梁益寧七州、後將軍、荊州刺史、假節，以桓脩為江州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict named Xuan supervisor of Jing, Si, Yong, Qin, Liang, Yi, Ning seven prefectures, General of the Rear, Inspector of Jingzhou, with credential authority, and made Huan Xiu Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court named him governor over seven western provinces as General of the Rear and inspector of Jingzhou with plenary powers, assigning Jiangzhou to Huan Xiu.

sentences.zh: 玄上疏固爭江州，於是進督八州及楊豫八郡，復領江州刺史。

translations.literal: Xuan memorialized to insist on Jiangzhou; he was then advanced to supervise eight prefectures and Yang and Yu eight commanderies, again holding Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan protested until the court expanded his mandate to eight provinces plus eight Yang–Yu commanderies and restored Jiangzhou to him.

sentences.zh: 玄又輒以偉為冠軍將軍、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Xuan further on his own authority made Wei General Who Conquers the Champion and Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Without permission he then named Huan Wei General Who Vanquishes the Enemy and governor of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 時寇賊未平，朝廷難違其意，許之。

translations.literal: At the time bandits and rebels were not yet pacified; the court found it hard to defy his intent and granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels still roiled the realm; the court could hardly refuse.

sentences.zh: 玄於是樹用腹心，兵馬日盛，屢上疏求討孫恩，詔輒不許。

translations.literal: Xuan then planted trusted men; his military strength grew daily; he repeatedly memorialized asking to campaign against Sun En; the edicts always refused.
translations.idiomatic: He packed offices with confidants while his armies swelled, pestering the throne for permission to crush Sun En—each edict refused.

sentences.zh: 其後恩逼京都，玄建牙聚眾，外托勤王，實欲觀釁而進，復上疏請討之。

translations.literal: Afterward En pressed the capital; Xuan raised his banner and gathered hosts, outwardly claiming to aid the king but actually wishing to watch for an opening to advance; he again memorialized asking to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun En threatened the capital, Xuan hoisted banners and massed troops, professing loyalty while watching for advantage, and again begged leave to strike.

sentences.zh: 會恩已走，玄又奉詔解嚴。

translations.literal: When En had already withdrawn, Xuan again received an edict lifting martial law.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sun En withdrew, another edict lifted mobilization.

sentences.zh: 以偉為江州，鎮夏口；

translations.literal: He assigned Wei to Jiangzhou, garrisoning Xiakou;
translations.idiomatic: He posted Huan Wei to Jiangzhou with headquarters at Xiakou;

sentences.zh: 司馬刁暢為輔國將軍，督八郡，鎮襄陽；

translations.literal: Sima Diao Chang as General Who Assists the State, supervising eight commanderies, garrisoning Xiangyang;
translations.idiomatic: named Sima Diao Chang General Who Supports the State over eight commanderies with base at Xiangyang;

sentences.zh: 遣桓振、皇甫敷、馮該等戍湓口。

translations.literal: he sent Huan Zhen, Huangfu Fu, Feng Gai, and others to guard Penkou.
translations.idiomatic: and detached Huan Zhen, Huangfu Fu, Feng Gai, and others to hold Penkou.

sentences.zh: 移沮漳蠻二千戶於江南，立武寧郡；

translations.literal: He relocated two thousand households of Ju–Zhang Man to south of the Yangzi and established Wuining commandery;
translations.idiomatic: He resettled two thousand Ju-Zhang barbarian households south of the river and formed Wuning commandery;

sentences.zh: 更招集流人，立綏安郡。

translations.literal: He further gathered floating migrants and established Sui'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He also settled displaced people and founded Sui'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 又置諸郡丞。

translations.literal: He also established assistant prefects for the commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He installed assistant prefects across those jurisdictions.

sentences.zh: 詔征廣州刺史刁逵、豫章太守郭昶之，玄皆留不遣。

translations.literal: An edict summoned Prefect of Guangzhou Diao Kui and Prefect of Yuzhang Guo Changzhi; Xuan detained them all and would not let them go.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Guangzhou governor Diao Kui and Yuzhang prefect Guo Changzhi to the capital; Xuan held every one of them back.

sentences.zh: 自謂三分有二，知勢運所歸，屢上禎祥以為己瑞。

translations.literal: He told himself that he held two of the tripartite realm, knew the mandate of fortune was his, and repeatedly reported auspicious omens as presages of himself.
translations.idiomatic: He fancied that two-thirds of the land was already his, that destiny favored him, and kept memorializing ill omens turned good as his own portents.

sentences.zh: 初。

translations.literal: At first.
translations.idiomatic: It began thus:

sentences.zh: 庾楷既奔于玄，玄之求討孫恩也，以為右將軍。

translations.literal: After Yu Kai had fled to Xuan, when Xuan sought to campaign against Sun En he appointed [Kai] General of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yu Kai had thrown in with Xuan, Xuan named him General of the Right for the proposed Sun En expedition.

sentences.zh: 玄既解嚴，楷亦去職。

translations.literal: Once Xuan lifted martial law, Kai likewise vacated his post.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan stood down mobilization, Kai resigned as well.

sentences.zh: 楷以玄方與朝廷構怨，恐事不克，禍及於己，乃密結于後將軍元顯，許為內應。

translations.literal: Kai supposed Xuan was still at odds with the court and feared the affair might fail and calamity reach himself; he therefore secretly allied with Rear General Sima Yuanxian and promised to act as inner collaborator.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Kai believed Xuan remained at war with Jiankang and worried that defeat would drag him down; he secretly dealt with Rear General Sima Yuanxian and offered inside help.

sentences.zh: 元興初，元顯稱詔伐玄，玄從兄石生時為太傅長史，密書報玄。

translations.literal: At the start of Yuanxing, Yuanxian declared an edict to attack Xuan; Xuan's elder cousin Shisheng then served as chief clerk to the Grand Tutor and sent a secret letter warning Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanxing, Yuanxian trumpeted orders to strike Xuan; Xuan's cousin Huan Shisheng, chief clerk to the Grand Tutor, slipped him warning.

sentences.zh: 玄本謂揚土饑饉，孫恩未滅，必未遑討己，可得蓄力養眾，觀釁而動。

translations.literal: Xuan had assumed that Yangzhou was starving and Sun En still undefeated—the court could not spare troops against him—so he could hoard strength, nurture troops, and move when a crack appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan counted on famine in Yangzhou and Sun En still raging, figuring the throne could not yet march west; he meant to gather strength and watch for an opening.

sentences.zh: 既聞元顯將伐之，甚懼，欲保江陵。

translations.literal: When he heard Yuanxian would attack, he was greatly afraid and wished to hold Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Yuanxian meant to move against him, he panicked and thought to dig in at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 長史卞范之說玄曰：「公英略威名振於天下，元顯口尚乳臭，劉牢之大失物情，若兵臨近畿，示以威賞，則土崩之勢可翹足而待，何有延敵入境自取蹙弱者乎！

translations.literal: Chief clerk Bian Fanzhi urged Xuan: "Your lordship's strategy and renown shake the realm; Yuanxian still reeks of milk; Liu Laozhi has lost all popular support; if you bring arms to the capital's edge and show both dread and reward, a rout can be had as easily as crossing legs—why stretch the enemy into your territory and pick the weak course!"
translations.idiomatic: Bian Fanzhi told Xuan, "You command awe across the land; Yuanxian is a child; Laozhi has forfeited every bond of loyalty. March to the suburbs, brandish reward and terror, and the court will fall apart without effort—why invite the foe inside and hand them the advantage?"

sentences.zh: 」玄大悅，乃留其兄偉守江陵，抗表率眾，下至尋陽，移檄京邑，罪狀元顯。

translations.literal: Xuan was greatly pleased; he left his brother Wei to guard Jiangling, raised the standard, led the host down to Xunyang, and sent a proclamation to the capital denouncing Yuanxian.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Xuan posted Wei at Jiangling, unfurled his banner, descended to Xunyang, and circulated a manifesto indicting Yuanxian.

sentences.zh: 檄至。

translations.literal: When the proclamation arrived.
translations.idiomatic: The manifesto reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 元顯大懼，下船而不克發。

translations.literal: Yuanxian was terrified; he boarded a boat but could not bring himself to cast off.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian quailed—he stepped aboard yet could not weigh anchor.

sentences.zh: 玄既失人情，而興師犯順，慮眾不為用，恆有回旆之計。

translations.literal: Although Xuan had forfeited popular sympathy by raising troops against legitimate authority, he worried the army might not obey and constantly planned to turn his banners back.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan knew he had alienated people by rebelling, doubted his troops would fight, and kept ready to wheel about and retreat.

sentences.zh: 既過尋陽，不見王師，意甚悅，其將吏亦振。

translations.literal: Once past Xunyang he saw no imperial army; his mood lifted greatly, and his officers likewise rallied.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond Xunyang he met no royal forces; relief surged through him and his commanders.

sentences.zh: 庾楷謀泄，收縶之。

translations.literal: Yu Kai's plot leaked; [Yuanxian] seized and bound him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Kai's conspiracy surfaced, Yuanxian clapped him in chains.

sentences.zh: 至姑孰，使其將馮該、苻宏、皇甫敷、索元等先攻譙王尚之。

translations.literal: Reaching Gushu, he first sent generals Feng Gai, Fu Hong, Huangfu Fu, Suo Yuan, and others to attack Prince of Qiao Wang Shangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: At Gushu he ordered Feng Gai, Fu Hong, Huangfu Fu, Suo Yuan, and others to strike Prince Shangzhi of Qiao first.

sentences.zh: 尚之敗。

translations.literal: Shangzhi was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi broke.

sentences.zh: 劉牢之遣子敬宣詣玄降。

translations.literal: Liu Laozhi sent his son Jingxuan to Xuan to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laozhi dispatched Liu Jingxuan to offer submission to Xuan.

sentences.zh: 玄至新亭，元顯自潰。

translations.literal: When Xuan reached Xinting, Yuanxian collapsed of his own accord.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's arrival at Xinting scattered Yuanxian without a fight.

sentences.zh: 玄入京師，矯詔曰：「義旗雲集，罪在元顯。

translations.literal: Xuan entered the capital and forged an edict saying: "Righteous banners gather like clouds; the guilt lies with Yuanxian.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Jiankang, Xuan counterfeited an edict: "Loyal hosts mass—the crime is Yuanxian's alone."

sentences.zh: 太傅已別有教，其解嚴息甲，以副義心。

translations.literal: The Grand Tutor has already issued separate instructions: stand down arms and armor to match this righteous intent.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Tutor has sent other orders—disband troops and lay aside weapons in keeping with that righteous aim."

sentences.zh: 」又矯詔加己總百揆，侍中、都督中外諸軍事、丞相、錄尚書事、揚州牧，領徐州刺史，又加假黃鉞、羽葆鼓吹、班劍二十人，置左右長史、司馬、從事中郎四人，甲杖二百人上殿。

translations.literal: "He further forged an edict promoting himself to oversee all offices of state: Palace Attendant, commander-in-chief of all military affairs within and without, chancellor, recorder of the Secretariat affairs, Yangzhou shepherd, concurrent Inspector of Xuzhou; further granted the yellow axe, feather-canopy band, palatial pipes, twenty sword attendants, four senior clerks and adjutants left and right, two hundred armored attendants allowed on the palace stairs.
translations.idiomatic: Another bogus edict named him overseer of every ministry—Palace Attendant, grand marshal of inner and outer armies, chancellor, chief of the Secretariat, Yangzhou governor with Xuzhou added, plus the golden axe, imperial pennons, a twenty-man sword escort, four chief clerks, and two hundred guards permitted on the hall steps.

sentences.zh: 玄表列太傅道子及元顯之惡，徙道子于安成郡，害元顯於市。

translations.literal: Xuan listed the Grand Tutor Daozi's and Yuanxian's crimes, banished Daozi to Ancheng commandery, and had Yuanxian killed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: He indicted Sima Daozi and his son, exiled the Grand Tutor to Ancheng, and executed Yuanxian in public.

sentences.zh: 於是玄入居太傅府，害太傅中郎毛泰、泰弟遊擊將軍邃，太傅參軍荀遜、前豫州刺史庾楷父子、吏部郎袁遵、譙王尚之等，流尚之弟丹陽尹恢之、廣晉伯允之、驃騎長史王誕、太傅主簿毛遁等於交廣諸郡，尋追害恢之、允之於道。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xuan moved into the Grand Tutor's mansion, murdered Palace Gentleman Mao Tai of the Grand Tutor's staff, Mao Tai's younger brother Mobile Corps general Mao Sui, Grand Tutor aide Xun Xun, former Inspector of Yuzhang Yu Kai with his son, Personnel Ministry secretary Yuan Zun, Prince of Qiao Wang Shangzhi, and others; he banished Shangzhi's younger brother Prefect of Danyang Yin Huizhi, Baron of Guangjin Yin Yunzhi, chief clerk of the Cavalry General Wang Dan, Grand Tutor registrar Mao Dun, and others to Jiao–Guang commanderies, then soon hunted Huizhi and Yunzhi down on the road and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Next he seized the Grand Tutor compound and slaughtered Mao Tai, Mao Sui, Xun Xun, the Yu Kai household, Yuan Zun, Prince Shangzhi, and more; he shipped Yin brothers and allied officials south before assassinating key exiles en route.

sentences.zh: 以兄偉為安西將軍、荊州刺史，領南蠻校尉，從兄謙為左僕射、加中軍將軍、領選，脩為右將軍、徐兗二州刺史，石生為前將軍、江州刺史，長史為卞範之為建武將軍、丹陽尹、王謐為中書令、領軍將軍。

translations.literal: He appointed his elder brother Wei General Who Guards the West and Inspector of Jingzhou with concurrent Southern Man colonel; elder cousin Qian as Junior Mentor with concurrent Central Army general and personnel selection; Xiu as General of the Right and inspector of Xu–Yan two prefectures; Shisheng as General of the Vanguard and Inspector of Jiangzhou; chief clerk Bian Fanzhi as General Who Establishes Might and prefect of Danyang; Wang Mi as Palace Writer with concurrent leader of the palace guards.
translations.idiomatic: Kin packed high posts: Huan Wei ruled Jingzhou; Huan Qian ran personnel; Huan Xiu held Xu-Yan; Huan Shisheng took Jiangzhou; Bian Fanzhi governed Danyang; Wang Mi commanded the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 大赦，改元為大亨。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed; the era name became Dahuan.
translations.idiomatic: He declared empire-wide amnesty and renamed the reign Dahang.

sentences.zh: 玄讓丞相，自署太尉、領平西將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Xuan yielded the chancellorship and instead titled himself Grand Commandant with concurrent General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned nominal chancellor yet styled himself Grand Commandant, Pacifier of the West, and governor of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 又加袞冕之服，綠糸戾綬，增班劍為六十人，劍履上殿，入朝不趨，贊奏不名。

translations.literal: Further added caul-and-mitre robes, green-li ribbons, increased sword attendants to sixty, permission to wear swords and shoes on the stairs, enter court without hurrying, and address the throne without giving personal name.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed robe-and-cap regalia, green cords, sixty sword pages, blade-on-steps privilege, unhurried audiences, and immunity from reciting his name.

sentences.zh: 玄將出居姑孰，訪之于眾，王謐對曰：「《公羊》有言，周公何以不之魯？

translations.literal: When Xuan was about to move his residence to Gushu he polled the assembly; Wang Mi replied: "The Gongyang Commentary asks why the Duke of Zhou did not go to Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Before relocating headquarters to Gushu Xuan polled ministers; Wang Mi answered with Gongyang: "Why did the Duke of Zhou stay away from Lu?"

sentences.zh: 欲天下一乎周也。

translations.literal: "He desires All-under-Heaven unified under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: "Because he wanted the realm unified through Zhou."

sentences.zh: 願靜根本，以公旦為心。

translations.literal: "I pray you quiet the root and take Duke Dan as your heart.
translations.idiomatic: "Anchor your base as Duke Dan anchored Zhou."

sentences.zh: 」玄善其對而不能從。

translations.literal: "Xuan praised the reply but could not follow it.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan applauded yet ignored the counsel.

sentences.zh: 遂大築城府，台館山池莫不壯麗，乃出鎮焉。

translations.literal: He therefore built ramparts, mansions, terraces, ponds—all magnificent—and went out to command from there.
translations.idiomatic: He threw up fortress walls, mansions, lakes—sumptuous—and ruled from Gushu.

sentences.zh: 既至姑孰，固辭錄尚書事，詔許之，而大政皆諮焉，小事則決於桓謙、卞範之。

translations.literal: Once at Gushu he firmly declined recorder of Secretariat affairs; an edict permitted it, yet great policy was still referred to him while trifles fell to Huan Qian and Bian Fanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: At Gushu he ostensibly refused the Secretariat recorder title—approved—but every weighty decision still passed his desk while Qian and Bian handled trivia.

sentences.zh: 自禍難屢構，干戈不戢，百姓厭之。

translations.literal: Because calamities piled up repeatedly and weapons never rested, the common people grew weary.
translations.idiomatic: Years of disaster and war had exhausted the people.

sentences.zh: 思歸一統。

translations.literal: They longed to return to unity.
translations.idiomatic: They hungered for reunification.

sentences.zh: 及玄初至也，黜凡佞，擢俊賢，君子之道粗備，京師欣然。

translations.literal: When Xuan first arrived he cashiered the vulgar flatterers and promoted worthy men—conduct fit for a gentleman was roughly in place—and the capital rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Xuan purged toadies, lifted talent—something like honest rule—and Jiankang welcomed him.

sentences.zh: 後乃陵侮朝廷，幽擯宰輔，豪奢縱欲，眾務繁興，於是朝野失望，人不安業。

translations.literal: Afterward he insulted the court, banished chief ministers, indulged extravagance and appetite, and piled on intrusive policies—thereupon court and countryside despaired and livelihoods turned insecure.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he humiliated the throne, expelled ministers, reveled in luxury, and churned out intrusive orders until hopes collapsed and trade stalled.

sentences.zh: 時會稽饑荒，玄令賑貸之。

translations.literal: At the time Kuaiji suffered famine; Xuan ordered relief loans.
translations.idiomatic: Kuaiji starved; Xuan commanded grain relief.

sentences.zh: 百姓散在江湖采穭，內史王愉悉召之還。

translations.literal: The common people scattered along rivers and lakes gathering wild grain; Prefect Wang Yu summoned them all back.
translations.idiomatic: Peasants had scattered harvesting shore grasses; Interior Prefect Wang Yu forced everyone home.

sentences.zh: 請米，米既不多，吏不時給，頓僕道路死者十八九焉。

translations.literal: They begged for grain—grain was scant and clerks issued it tardily—many collapsed dead along the roads, eight or nine in ten.
translations.idiomatic: They pleaded for rice—stores ran low and clerks delayed distribution—so corpses lined the roads, nearly everyone dying.

sentences.zh: 玄又害吳興太守高素、輔國將軍竺謙之、謙之從兄高平相朗之、輔國將軍劉襲、襲弟彭城內史季武、冠軍將軍孫無終等，皆牢之之黨，北府舊將也。

translations.literal: Xuan further killed Prefect of Wuxing Gao Su, General Who Assists the State Zhu Qianzhi, Zhu Qianzhi's elder cousin Administrator of Gaoping Lang Zhu, General Who Assists the State Liu Xi, Liu Xi's younger brother Interior Prefect of Pengcheng Ji Wu, General Who Conquers the Champion Sun Wuzhong, and others—all Liu Laozhi's faction, veterans of the northern headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He next murdered northern-command cohort—Gao Su, Zhu Qianzhi, Zhu Langzhi, Liu Xi, Liu Ji Wu, Sun Wuzhong—everyone tied to Liu Laozhi.

sentences.zh: 襲兄冀州刺史軌及甯朔將軍高雅之、牢之子敬宣並奔慕容德。

translations.literal: Liu Xi's elder brother Inspector of Jizhou Gui together with General Who Calms the North Gao Yazhi and Laozhi's son Jingxuan fled to Murong De.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gui, Gao Yazhi, and Liu Jingxuan bolted to Southern Yan's Murong De.

sentences.zh: 玄諷朝廷以己平元顯功，封豫章公，食安成郡地方二百二十五里，邑七千五百戶；

translations.literal: Xuan prompted the court that his merit in pacifying Yuanxian merited fief as Duke of Yuzhang with territory of Ancheng commandery two hundred twenty-five li square and seven thousand five hundred households;
translations.idiomatic: He coached edicts rewarding himself Duke of Yuzhang—two hundred twenty-five li of Ancheng grain lands and seventy-five hundred households;

sentences.zh: 平仲堪、佺期功，封桂陽郡公，地方七十五里，邑二千五百戶；

translations.literal: for merit in pacifying Zhongkan and Quanqi, fief as Duke of Guiyang commandery seventy-five li square and twenty-five hundred households;
translations.idiomatic: plus another dukedom at Guiyang—seventy-five li and twenty-five hundred mouths—for defeating Yin Zhongkan and Yang Quanqi;

sentences.zh: 本封南郡如故。

translations.literal: his original Nanjun ducal title remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: the old Nanjun dukedom stayed untouched.

sentences.zh: 玄以豫章改封息升，桂陽郡公賜兄子浚，降為西道縣公。

translations.literal: Xuan reassigned the Yuzhang dukedom to his son Sheng; gave the Guiyang dukedom to nephew Jun; reduced [another branch] to Duke of Xidao county.
translations.idiomatic: He handed Yuzhang to his son Huan Sheng, Guiyang to nephew Huan Jun, and trimmed collateral heirs to county rank.

sentences.zh: 又發詔為桓溫諱，有姓名同者一皆改之，贈其母馬氏豫章公太夫人。

translations.literal: He further issued an edict enforcing taboo on Huan Wen's name—all who shared it must change—and posthumously titled his mother Lady Ma Grand Duchess of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: He forbade anyone to bear Wen's name like his father and honored Lady Ma as dowager duchess.

sentences.zh: 元興二年，玄詐表請平姚興，又諷朝廷作詔，不許。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanxing Xuan feigned a memorial asking to pacify Yao Xing; he also coached the court to respond with refusal.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxing II saw Xuan fake a western campaign petition while prompting refusal from the throne.

sentences.zh: 玄本無資力，而好為大言，既不克行，乃雲奉詔故止。

translations.literal: Xuan lacked resources yet loved grand pronouncements; unable to launch the expedition he claimed an edict made him stop.
translations.idiomatic: Cash-stricken but boastful, he blamed imperial orders when nothing marched.

sentences.zh: 初欲飾裝，無他處分，先使作輕舸，載服玩及書畫等物。

translations.literal: When first intending to outfit supplies he had no other arrangement—he first ordered light boats loaded with wardrobe curios and scroll paintings.
translations.idiomatic: Planning baggage trains, he prioritized barges of robes, curios, and calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 或諫之，玄曰：「書畫服玩既宜恆在左右，且兵凶戰危，脫有不意，當使輕而易運。

translations.literal: Some remonstrated; Xuan said: "Paintings and wardrobe curios should stay at one's side; moreover arms are ill-omened—should mishap strike they must be easy to haul.
translations.idiomatic: Critics objected; Xuan retorted, "Art and wardrobe belong beside me; war is peril—if disaster strikes I must travel light."

sentences.zh: 」眾咸笑之。

translations.literal: All laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone mocked him.

sentences.zh: 是歲，玄兄偉卒，贈開府、驃騎將軍，以桓脩代之。

translations.literal: That year Xuan's elder brother Wei died; posthumous honors reached opener-of-office and Cavalry General; Huan Xiu succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei died Xuan piled titles on him and slid Huan Xiu into his place.

sentences.zh: 從事中郎曹靖之說玄以桓脩兄弟職居內外，恐權傾天下，玄納之，乃以南郡相桓石康為西中郎將、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Adjutant Cao Jingzhi warned Xuan that Huan Xiu's brothers held inner and outer posts and might monopolize power; Xuan accepted it and therefore named Administrator of Nanjun Huan Shikang General Who Guards the West and Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jingzhi feared the Xiu brothers spanning palace and camps; Xuan listened and posted Huan Shikang over Jingzhou instead.

sentences.zh: 偉服始以公除，玄便作樂。

translations.literal: When Wei mourning first ended by public notice Xuan held music.
translations.idiomatic: The moment Wei's mourning lifted Xuan threw banquets.

sentences.zh: 初奏，玄撫節慟哭，既而收淚盡歡，玄所親仗唯偉，偉既死，玄乃孤危。

translations.literal: At the first strike of the musicians Xuan gripped the baton and wailed in grief; presently he wiped tears and reveled—those Xuan relied on were only Wei; once Wei died Xuan stood isolated.
translations.idiomatic: Music began with theatrical tears, then feasting—Wei had been his lone pillar; without Wei he teetered.

sentences.zh: 而不臣之跡已著，自知怨滿天下，欲速定篡逆，殷仲文、卞範之等又共催促之，於是先改授群司，解琅邪王司徒，遷太宰，加殊禮，以桓謙為侍中、衛將軍、開府、錄尚書事，王謐散騎常侍、中書監，領司徒，桓胤中書令，加桓脩散騎常侍、撫軍大將軍。

translations.literal: Yet traces of disloyalty already showed; knowing resentment filled the realm he wished to hurry usurpation—Yin Zhongwen, Bian Fanzhi, and others urged him on—therefore he first reshuffled all offices, removing Prince of Langye from Minister of Education to Grand Tutor with extraordinary honors, naming Huan Qian Palace Attendant, Guards general, opener-of-office, recorder of Secretariat; Wang Mi senior attendant and Palace Writer with concurrent Minister of Education; Huan Yin Palace Writer; adding Huan Xiu senior attendant and General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing mutiny inevitable and hatred empire-wide, Xuan rushed toward coup—Zhongwen and Bian pressed—so he reshuffled ministers, bumped Prince of Langye to Grand Tutor, stacked Qian, Wang Mi, Yin, Xiu across key seals.

sentences.zh: 置學官，教授二品子弟數百人。

translations.literal: He established academies and enrolled several hundred sons of second-rank houses as students.
translations.idiomatic: He opened schools for hundreds of elite youths.

sentences.zh: 又矯詔加其相國，總百揆，封南郡、南平、宜都、天門、零陵、營陽、桂陽、衡陽、義陽、建平十郡為楚王，揚州牧，領平西將軍、豫州刺史如故，加九錫備物，楚國置丞相已下，一遵舊典。

translations.literal: He further forged an edict naming himself prince of Chu with powers of chief minister over all offices, enfeoffing ten commanderies—Nanjun, Nanping, Yidu, Tianmen, Lingling, Yingyang, Guiyang, Hengyang, Yiyang, Jianping—as Prince of Chu, Yangzhou shepherd, concurrent General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yuzhou as before, plus the nine bestowals in full; Chu state replicated Han precedent from chancellor downward.
translations.idiomatic: Another fake edict crowned him Chu prince over ten commanderies, Yangzhou governor, western pacifier, Yuzhou inspector, nine insignia, full Chu bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 又諷天子御前殿而策授焉。

translations.literal: He also coached the Son of Heaven to convene in the forward hall and conduct the investiture.
translations.idiomatic: He staged an audience where the emperor handed him the patent.

sentences.zh: 玄屢偽讓，詔遣百僚敦勸，又云：「當親降鑾輿乃受命。

translations.literal: Xuan repeatedly declined in pretense; edicts sent the hundred officials to press him; he also said: "I shall accept only when the imperial carriage comes in person.
translations.idiomatic: He played coy until ministers mobbed him with rehearsed pleas, insisting he would accept only if the emperor's coach descended."

sentences.zh: 」矯詔贈父溫為楚王，南康公主為楚王后。

translations.literal: "He forged an edict posthumously making his father Wen Prince of Chu and Princess Nankang Queen of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Forged honors raised late Huan Wen to Chu prince and Princess Nankang to queen.

sentences.zh: 以平西長史劉瑾為尚書，刁逵為中領軍，王嘏為太常，殷叔文為左衛，皇甫敷為右衛，凡眾官合六十餘人，為楚官屬。

translations.literal: He named Chief Clerk of Pacify-the-West Liu Jin Master of Writing, Diao Kui Central Garrison commander, Wang Jia Minister of Ceremonies, Yin Shuwen Guards of the Left, Huangfu Fu Guards of the Right—more than sixty posts become Chu staff.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty-odd offices became Chu ministry—Liu Jin, Diao Kui, Wang Jia, Yin Shuwen, Huangfu Fu among them.

sentences.zh: 玄解平西、豫州，以平西文武配相國府。

translations.literal: Xuan relinquished Pacify-the-West and Yuzhou, assigning those western civil and military officers to the prince-chancellor's bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He folded his western headquarters into the Chu chancellery.

sentences.zh: 新野人庾仄聞玄受九錫，乃起義兵，襲馮該於襄陽，走之。

translations.literal: A man of Xinye, Yu Ze, hearing Xuan received the nine bestowals, raised loyal troops and struck Feng Gai at Xiangyang, putting him to flight.
translations.idiomatic: When Xinye's Yu Ze heard the nine honors he attacked Feng Gai at Xiangyang and routed him.

sentences.zh: 仄有眾七千，于城南設壇，祭祖宗七廟。

translations.literal: Ze had seven thousand men; south of the city he raised an altar and sacrificed to seven generations of ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Seven thousand strong, he sacrificed south of Xiangyang to seven ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 南蠻參軍庾彬、安西參軍楊道護、江安令鄧襄子謀為內應。

translations.literal: Southern Man aide Yu Bin, Pacify-the-West aide Yang Daohu, and Jiang'an magistrate Deng Xiangzi plotted inner collaboration.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bin, Yang Daohu, and Deng Xiangzi planned internal support.

sentences.zh: 仄本仲堪黨，桓偉既死，石康未至，故乘間而發，江陵震動。

translations.literal: Ze had been Zhongkan's partisan; Huan Wei was dead and Shikang not yet arrived—he exploited the gap and struck; Jiangling trembled.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Ze had backed Yin Zhongkan; with Wei gone and Shikang absent he seized the moment, rocking Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 桓濟之子亮起兵于羅縣，自號平南將軍、湘州刺史，以討仄為名。

translations.literal: Huan Ji's son Liang raised troops at Luo county, styled himself Pacifier of the South and Inspector of Xiangzhou, citing campaign against Ze.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Liang mustered Luo county as "Pacifier of the South" to crush Yu Ze.

sentences.zh: 南蠻校尉羊僧壽與石康共攻襄陽，仄眾散，奔姚興，彬等皆遇害。

translations.literal: Southern Man colonel Yang Shoushou with Shikang jointly attacked Xiangyang; Ze's host scattered and he fled to Yao Xing; Bin and the others were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shoushou and Shikang took Xiangyang; Yu Ze fled to Later Qin; conspirators died.

sentences.zh: 長沙相陶延壽以亮乘亂起兵，遣收之。

translations.literal: Prefect of Changsha Tao Yanshou, deeming Liang exploited turmoil to revolt, sent agents to seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Changsha's Tao Yanshou arrested Liang for rabble-raising.

sentences.zh: 玄徙亮於衡陽，誅其同謀桓奧等。

translations.literal: Xuan banished Liang to Hengyang and executed fellow plotters including Huan Ao.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan exiled Liang to Hengyang and killed co-conspirators such as Huan Ao.

sentences.zh: 玄偽上表求歸籓，又自作詔留之，遣使宣旨，玄又上表固請，又諷天子作手詔固留焉。

translations.literal: Xuan forged a memorial begging return to his fief, then forged an edict detaining him; he sent envoys to proclaim intent; Xuan again memorialized insisting; he coached the emperor to hand-copy edicts pressing him to stay.
translations.idiomatic: He scripted resignations, scripted counter-edicts to refuse, scripted fresh pleas—pure theater.

sentences.zh: 玄好逞偽辭，塵穢簡牘，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Xuan loved hollow rhetoric; documents grew filthy with such deceit—all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in counterfeit petitions that cluttered every inbox.

sentences.zh: 謂代謝之際宜有禎祥，乃密令所在上臨平湖開除清朗，使眾官集賀。

translations.literal: Deciding a dynastic transition ought to show omens, he secretly ordered locales to report Linping Lake cleared and bright, then assembled officials to congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: Wanting omens for usurpation, he rigged reports that Linping Lake had cleared and staged mass congratulations.

sentences.zh: 矯詔曰：「靈瑞之事非所敢聞也。

translations.literal: "He forged an edict saying: "We dare not hear talk of numinous portents.
translations.idiomatic: A bogus edict sniffed, "We should not hear such miracles."

sentences.zh: 斯誠相國至德，故事為之應。

translations.literal: "This truly reflects the chief minister's supreme virtue—story responds accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: "Yet they arise from the chief minister's virtue—history echoes him."

sentences.zh: 太平之化，於是乎始，六合同悅，情何可言！

translations.literal: "Great Peace's transformation begins here; the six directions rejoice together—what words can convey it!"
translations.idiomatic: "Harmony begins; all under heaven rejoices—beyond words!"

sentences.zh: 」又詐云江州甘露降王成基家竹上。

translations.literal: "He further falsely announced sweet dew in Jiangzhou falling on Wang Chengji's bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: He also faked sweet dew on Wang Chengji's bamboo in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 玄以歷代咸有肥遁之士，而己世獨無，乃征皇甫謐六世孫希之為著作，並給其資用，皆令讓而不受，號曰高士，時人名為「充隱」。

translations.literal: Because past dynasties all had recluses yet his age had none, he summoned Huangfu Mi's sixth-generation descendant Xizhi as editorial clerk, supplied expenses, had him decline everything—styled "Lofty Gentleman"; contemporaries dubbed him "stuffed recluse."
translations.idiomatic: Unable to find hermits, he press-ganged Huangfu Xizhi into a staged refusal of salary—the "supplemental recluse."

sentences.zh: 議復肉刑，斷錢貨，回復改異，造革紛紜，志無一定，條制森然，動害政理。

translations.literal: He debated restoring corporal punishment, abolishing coinage, reversing reforms—endless noisy schemes, mind never settled; regulations proliferated and harmed governance.
translations.idiomatic: He toggled between mutilation law, currency bans, policy reversals—chaotic rules that paralyzed government.

sentences.zh: 性貪鄙，好奇異，尤愛寶物，珠玉不離於手。

translations.literal: By nature greedy and base, he craved curios and loved treasures—pearls and jade never left his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Voracious and vulgar, he fondled gems constantly.

sentences.zh: 人士有法書好畫及佳園宅者，悉欲歸己，猶難逼奪之，皆蒱博而取。

translations.literal: Notables with fine calligraphy, paintings, or gardens—he wanted them all; loath to seize openly—he won them through gambling.
translations.idiomatic: He coveted art and estates but dice games masked seizure.

sentences.zh: 遣臣佐四出，掘果移竹，不遠數千里，百姓佳果美竹無復遺餘。

translations.literal: He sent aides in every direction to dig up fruit trees and transplant bamboo—thousands of li—until no choice orchard or bamboo grove remained for commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Agents uprooted prize fruit and bamboo across provinces until locals had nothing left.

sentences.zh: 信悅諂譽，逆忤讜言，或奪其所憎與其所愛。

translations.literal: He trusted flattery, punished straight speech—stripping foes and gifting favorites.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded sycophants, punished candor, confiscated from hated houses and gifted allies.

sentences.zh: 十一月，玄矯制加其冕十有二旒，建天子旌旗，出警入蹕，乘金根車，駕六馬，備五時副車，置旄頭雲罕，樂儛八佾，設鐘虡宮縣，妃為王后，世子為太子，其女及孫爵命之號皆如舊制。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Xuan forged orders adding twelve tassels to his crown, raising imperial pennants, outer alarm and inner clearing escorts, riding the golden-root carriage with six horses, five-season duplicate coaches, yak-tail and cloud pennons, eight rows of dancers, bell racks and suspended chimes in the palace mode; his consort became queen, heir son crown prince—titles for daughters and grandsons followed old statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month: counterfeit regalia—twelve-crown tassels, imperial banners, full motorcade, six-horse chariot, ritual dancers, palace music; wife elevated queen, son heir—noble ladies titled per Jin law.

sentences.zh: 玄乃多斥朝臣為太宰僚佐，又矯詔使王謐兼太保，領司徒，奉皇帝璽禪位於己。

translations.literal: Xuan cashiered many courtiers into Grand Tutor staff; forged edict making Wang Mi concurrent Grand Guardian and Minister of Education to present the imperial seal and abdicate to himself.
translations.idiomatic: He demoted ministers into Grand Tutor hangers-on and scripted Wang Mi handing him the jade seal.

sentences.zh: 又諷帝以禪位告廟，出居永安宮，移晉神主於琅邪廟。

translations.literal: He also coached the emperor to announce abdication at the temple, move out to Yongan Palace, and shift Jin spirit tablets to the Langye temple.
translations.idiomatic: He staged abdication rites, packed the emperor off to Yongan, and relocated ancestral tablets to Langye shrine.

sentences.zh: 初，玄恐帝不肯為手詔，又慮璽不可得，逼臨川王寶請帝自為手詔，因奪取璽。

translations.literal: At first Xuan feared the emperor would refuse a handwritten edict and worried the seal might not be had—he pressed Prince of Linchuan Bao to make the emperor write personally, then seized the seal.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing refusal, he forced Prince Bao to extract an autograph edict and snatched the seal.

sentences.zh: 比臨軒，璽已久出，玄甚喜。

translations.literal: By the time of the audience the seal was long out—Xuan was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Come audience day the seal already sat in his hands—Xuan exulted.

sentences.zh: 百官到姑孰勸玄僭偽位，玄偽讓，朝臣固請，玄乃于城南七里立郊，登壇篡位，以玄牡告天，百僚陪列，而儀注不備，忘稱萬歲，又不易帝諱。

translations.literal: When the hundred officials reached Gushu urging Xuan to take the usurped throne, Xuan feigned refusal; courtiers pressed again; Xuan then raised an altar seven li south of the city, ascended, usurped the throne, reported to Heaven with a black bull; the hundred officials attended but ritual texts were incomplete—forgot to shout "ten thousand years" and did not change the Jin emperor's taboo name.
translations.idiomatic: Officials begged him south of Gushu; after scripted refusals he built an altar, mounted it, declared himself emperor, sacrificed black ox—but botched ritual: no "long live," no taboo update.

sentences.zh: 榜為文告天皇后帝云：「晉帝欽若景運，敬順明命，以命于玄。

translations.literal: The board text announced to Heaven empress and emperor said: "The Jin emperor reverently follows bright fortune and obeys the clarified mandate, thereby commanding Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Placards claimed: "The Jin sovereign reveres destiny and orders Huan Xuan to succeed."

sentences.zh: 夫天工人代，帝王所以興，匪君莫治，惟德司其元，故承天理物，必由一統。

translations.literal: "Heaven's work is done by men—the reason emperors arise; without a lord nothing is governed; only virtue masters the origin—therefore inheriting Heaven and ordering things must proceed through unity.
translations.idiomatic: "Heaven tasks mankind—thus dynasties rise; without virtuous master there is no rule—succession must unify the mandate."

sentences.zh: 並聖不可以二君，非賢不可以無主，故世換五帝，鼎遷三代。

translations.literal: "Two sages cannot coexist; without worthies there is no ruler—therefore ages shifted the Five Thearchs and the tripartite cauldrons moved through three dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: "Twin sagely lines cannot share one throne; ages rotated the Five Thearchs and Xia-Shang-Zhou passed the cauldrons."

sentences.zh: 爰暨漢魏，咸歸勳烈。

translations.literal: "Down to Han and Wei merit alone decided succession.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Wei alike enthroned merit.

sentences.zh: 晉自中葉，仍世多故，海西之亂，皇祚殆移，九代廓寧之功，升明黜陟之勳，微禹之德，左衽將及。

translations.literal: "From mid-Jin onward generations knew many troubles—Haixi's turmoil nearly shifted the imperial line; the merit that cleared nine reigns and the promotions that defined Shengming—without Yu's virtue we should have buttoned robes left-sided.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-Jin chaos—Prince Yi's deposition nearly ended the line—Nine-reign restoration and Shengming reforms alone, like Great Yu's floodwork, kept civilization from barbarian dress.

sentences.zh: 太元之末，君子道消，積釁基亂。

translations.literal: Toward the end of Taiyuan the way of gentlemen faded and accumulated rifts laid chaos's foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Late Taiyuan saw decent men silenced and old grudges seed rebellion.

sentences.zh: 鐘于隆安，禍延士庶，理絕人倫。

translations.literal: It struck in Long'an; calamity spread to gentry and commoners alike; principle sundered human relations.
translations.idiomatic: Long'an brought disaster to every class and shattered moral bonds.

sentences.zh: 玄雖身在草澤，見棄時班，義情理感，胡能無慨！

translations.literal: Although Xuan dwelt in the grasslands and was cast from official ranks, duty and feeling stirred him—how could he remain unmoved!
translations.idiomatic: Banished to common life yet stirred by justice, how could he withhold passion?

sentences.zh: 投袂克清之勞，阿衡撥亂之績，皆仰憑先德遺愛之利，玄何功焉！

translations.literal: The labor of casting aside sleeves to purge the realm, the achievement of the Regent who righted chaos—all leaned on the profit of late virtue's lingering grace—what merit had Xuan!
translations.idiomatic: Purging traitors and steadying the throne rested on his father's legacy—Xuan claimed no credit.

sentences.zh: 屬當理運之會，猥集樂推之數，以寡昧之身踵下武之重，膺革泰之始，托王公之上，誠仰藉洪基，德漸有由。

translations.literal: Just as the ordering fortune convened and the multitude's willing push gathered, with my dull self I tread the heavy mantle of martial succession, mount the Tai renewal's beginning, mount above the kings and dukes—truly I lean on the vast foundation; virtue's gradual spread has its source.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune aligned and acclaim gathered; though unworthy he assumed martial succession, mounted reform, and ruled above princes—borrowing his father's foundation.

sentences.zh: 夕惕祗懷，罔知攸厝。

translations.literal: Evening vigil and reverent breast—I know not where to rest.
translations.idiomatic: He feigned dread and reverence—nowhere to settle his heart.

sentences.zh: 君位不可以久虛，人神不可以乏饗，是用敢不奉以欽恭大禮，敬簡良辰，升壇受禪，告類上帝，以永綏眾望，式孚萬邦，惟明靈是饗。

translations.literal: The lord's seat cannot long stand empty; gods and men cannot lack sacrifice—therefore I dare not refuse the august great rite; respectfully I choose an auspicious day, ascend the altar, receive abdication, announce kindred to High Heaven, to eternally soothe mass expectation, to win all states—may bright spirits feast.
translations.idiomatic: Throne and sacrifices demand a ruler—so he staged abdication, chose a day, ascended the altar, and announced heaven.

sentences.zh: 」乃下書曰：「夫三才相資，天人所以成功，理由一統，貞夫所以司契，帝王之興，其源深矣。

translations.literal: "Thereupon he issued a document saying: "The three powers mutually sustain—thereby Heaven and man accomplish achievement; principle rests in unity—the steadfast thereby holds the tally; emperors rise—their source runs deep.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed that heaven-earth-man cooperate, legitimacy demands unity, and imperial ascent runs deep.

sentences.zh: 自三五已降，世代參差，雖所由或殊，其歸一也。

translations.literal: From the Three Five onward generations staggered; although paths differed, their end was one.
translations.idiomatic: Since mythic ages dynasties varied yet converged on one mandate.

sentences.zh: 朕皇考宣武王聖德高邈，誕啟洪基，景命攸歸，理貫自昔。

translations.literal: My august father King Xuanwu's sagely virtue towered high—he opened the grand foundation; bright mandate attached—principle threaded from antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: His father King Xuanwu opened the great enterprise and bore heaven's charge.

sentences.zh: 中間屯險，弗克負荷，仰瞻巨集業，殆若綴旒。

translations.literal: Amid peril we could not bear the burden; gazing up at the vast enterprise it hung like tassels on a crown.
translations.idiomatic: Hard years nearly broke them; the legacy seemed precarious as dangling threads.

sentences.zh: 藉否終之運，遇時來之會，用獲除奸救溺，拯拔人倫。

translations.literal: Borrowing the fortune of obstruction's end, encountering the hour's arrival, we obtained removal of traitors and rescue from drowning—lifting human relations.
translations.idiomatic: Through reversal's luck and timely union he purged rebels and rescued society.

sentences.zh: 晉氏以多難薦臻，歷數唯既，典章唐虞之准，述遵漢魏之則，用集天祿於朕躬。

translations.literal: The Jin house through many hardships reached its allotted span; modeling Tang–Yu standards and following Han–Wei precedents, Heaven's blessing settled on my person.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's mandate exhausted; modeling Yao-Shun and Han-Wei forms, he claimed the celestial salary.

sentences.zh: 惟德不敏，辭不獲命，稽若令典，遂升壇燎於南郊，受終於文祖。

translations.literal: Virtuous though I am not keen, declining met no approval; examining the canon I ascended the southern-suburb altar and received termination at the Pattern Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Feigning modesty yet obeying ritual, he burned offerings at the southern altar and received abdication at Wenzu temple.

sentences.zh: 思覃斯慶，願與億兆聿茲更始。

translations.literal: Thinking to extend this blessing, I wish with hundred millions to renew together.
translations.idiomatic: He vowed renewal with the myriad people.

sentences.zh: 」於是大赦，改元永始，賜天下爵二級，孝悌力田人三級，鰥寡孤獨不能自存者穀人五斛。

translations.literal: "Thereupon a general amnesty; era name became Yongshi; the realm received two noble ranks; filial, brotherly, diligent farmers three ranks; widowers, widows, orphans, childless unable to survive received five hu of grain each.
translations.idiomatic: He declared amnesty, renamed the reign Yongshi, raised ranks, and granted grain to the destitute.

sentences.zh: 其賞賜之制，徒設空文，無其實也。

translations.literal: As for the reward system—only empty text existed; there was no substance.
translations.idiomatic: The promised largesse stayed ink on paper—nothing real.

sentences.zh: 初出偽詔，改年為建始，右丞王悠之曰：「建始，趙王倫偽號也。

translations.literal: When first issuing forged edicts he changed the year to Jianshi; Right Assistant Wang Youzhi said: "Jianshi was the false reign name of Prince Zhao Lun."
translations.idiomatic: His first bogus era Jianshi echoed Sima Lun's usurpation—Wang Youzhi protested.

sentences.zh: 」又改為永始，復是王莽始執權之歲，其兆號不祥，冥符僭逆如此。

translations.literal: "It was again changed to Yongshi—again the year Wang Mang first seized power—such omens were ill; dark tokens matched usurpation thus.
translations.idiomatic: Renaming Yongshi replayed Wang Mang's opening year—another ill omen.

sentences.zh: 又下書曰：「夫三恪作賓，有自來矣。

translations.literal: He further issued a document: "The three guest houses have served as hosts since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: He invoked the classical "three guest" enfeoffments for former dynasties.

sentences.zh: 爰暨漢魏，咸建疆宇。

translations.literal: Down to Han and Wei each carved its territory.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Wei alike granted their royal houses domains.

sentences.zh: 晉氏欽若歷數，禪位於朕躬，宜則是古訓，授茲茅土。

translations.literal: The Jin house reverently followed the chronology and abdicated to my person—should model ancient instruction and award these fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Jin yielded the throne—he must enfeoff them per precedent.

sentences.zh: 以南康之平固縣奉晉帝為平固王，車旗正朔一如舊典。

translations.literal: Use Pinggu county of Nanjun to support the Jin emperor as Prince of Pinggu—chariots, banners, calendar as old statutes.
translations.idiomatic: He demoted the Jin emperor to Prince of Pinggu at Pinggu with former princely honors.

sentences.zh: 」遷帝居尋陽，即陳留王處鄴宮故事。

translations.literal: "He moved the emperor to lodge at Xunyang—following the precedent of Prince of Chenliu at Ye palace.
translations.idiomatic: He banished the emperor to Xunyang like Cao-Wei's puppet prince.

sentences.zh: 降永安皇后為零陵君，琅邪王為石陽縣公，武陵王遵為彭澤縣侯。

translations.literal: He reduced Empress Yongan to Lady of Lingling, Prince of Langye to Duke of Shiyang county, Prince Zun of Wuling to Marquis of Pengze county.
translations.idiomatic: He stripped titles from the empress and Sima princes to county nobility.

sentences.zh: 追尊其父溫宣武皇帝，廟稱太廟，南康公主為宣皇后。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored his father Wen as Emperor Xuanwu with temple name Grand Temple; Princess Nankang became Empress Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He canonized Huan Wen as Emperor Xuanwu and Princess Nankang as empress.

sentences.zh: 封子升為豫章郡王，叔父雲孫放之為甯都縣王，豁孫稚玉為臨沅縣王，豁次子石康為右將軍、武陵郡王，秘子蔚為醴陵縣王，贈沖太傳、宣城郡王，加殊禮，依晉安平王 故事，以孫胤襲爵，為吏部尚書，沖次子謙為揚州刺史、新安郡王，謙弟脩為撫軍大將軍、安成郡王，兄歆臨賀縣王，禕富陽縣王，贈偉侍中、大將軍、義興郡王，以子浚襲爵，為輔國將軍，浚弟邈西昌縣王。
