translations.literal: He enfeoffed his son Sheng as Prince of Yuzhang commandery; uncle Yun's grandson Fangzhi as Prince of Ningdu county; Heo's grandson Zhiyu as Prince of Linqi county; He's second son Shikang as General of the Right, Prince of Wuling commandery; Mi's son Wei as Prince of Liling county; posthumously awarded Chong Grand Tutor, Prince of Xuancheng with extraordinary rites, per Prince Anping of Jin precedent, grandson Yin inheriting title as Master of Writing; Chong's second son Qian as Yangzhou governor, Prince of Xin'an; Qian's younger brother Xiu as General Who Pacifies the Army, Prince of Ancheng; elder brother Xin Prince of Linhe county, Yi Prince of Fuyang county; posthumous Wei as Palace Attendant, Grand General, Prince of Yixing, son Jun inheriting as General Who Assists the State, Jun's younger brother Miao Prince of Xichang county.
translations.idiomatic: A flurry of princely titles: Huan Sheng and kin across the clan—Huan Shikang, Huan Wei, Huan Qian, Huan Xiu, and posthumous honors to Huan Chong, Huan Wei, with sons and nephews ennobled per convoluted Jin parallel.

sentences.zh: 封王謐為武昌公，班劍二十人，卞範之為臨汝公，殷仲文為東興公，馮該為魚復侯。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed Wang Mi as Duke of Wuchang with twenty sword attendants; Bian Fanzhi as Duke of Linru; Yin Zhongwen as Duke of Dongxing; Feng Gai as Marquis of Yufu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi became Duke of Wuchang; Bian Fanzhi Linru; Zhongwen Dongxing; Feng Gai marquis of Yufu.

sentences.zh: 又降始安郡公為縣公，長沙為臨湘縣公，盧陵為巴丘縣公，各千戶。

translations.literal: He further reduced Duke of Shian commandery to county duke, Changsha to Duke of Linxiang county, Luling to Duke of Baqiu county—each one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery dukedoms shrank to county-level fiefs at one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 其康樂、武昌、南昌、望蔡、建興、永脩、觀陽皆降封百戶，公侯之號如故。

translations.literal: As for Kangle, Wuchang, Nanchang, Wangcai, Jianxing, Yongxiu, Guanyang—all reduced to hundred-household fiefs; duke and marquis titles stayed.
translations.idiomatic: Other noble domains shrank to token hundred-household grants while titles lingered.

sentences.zh: 又普進諸征鎮軍號各有差。

translations.literal: He also promoted various expeditionary and garrison generalships by graded steps.
translations.idiomatic: Expeditionary ranks climbed by staged promotions.

sentences.zh: 以相國左長史王綏為中書令。

translations.literal: He named chief clerk of the prince-chancellor's left Wang Sui Palace Writer.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sui took the Palace Writer seal.

sentences.zh: 崇桓謙母庾氏為宣城太妃，加殊禮，給以輦乘。

translations.literal: He honored Huan Qian's mother Lady Yu as Grand Dowager of Xuancheng with extraordinary rites and supplied palanquin transport.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's mother Lady Yu became dowager of Xuancheng with carriage honors.

sentences.zh: 號溫墓曰永崇陵，置守衛四十人。

translations.literal: He styled Wen's tomb Eternal Reverence Mausoleum with forty guardians.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen's tomb was renamed Yongchong with a forty-man guard.

sentences.zh: 玄入建康宮，逆風迅激，旍旗儀飾皆傾偃。

translations.literal: When Xuan entered Jiankang Palace a fierce headwind struck; pennants and regalia all blew flat.
translations.idiomatic: Entering the palace a gale flattened banners and ritual gear.

sentences.zh: 及小會於西堂，設妓樂，殿上施絳綾帳，縷黃金為顏，四角作金龍，頭銜五色羽葆旒蘇，群臣竊相謂曰：「此頗似輀車，亦王莽仙蓋之流也。

translations.literal: When they held a minor banquet in the western hall with musicians and crimson damask hangings on the hall, gold thread forming faces, golden dragons at four corners holding five-colored plume canopies with tassels, ministers whispered: "This rather resembles a hearse—also Wang Mang's 'immortal canopy' sort."
translations.idiomatic: West-hall banquet with gold-thread curtains and dragon canopy corners reminded ministers of funeral wagons and Wang Mang's omens.

sentences.zh: 龍角，所謂亢龍有悔者也。

translations.literal: Dragon horns—what is called 'proud dragon has remorse.'"
translations.idiomatic: They muttered about "the soaring dragon's regret"—ill augury.

sentences.zh: 」又造金根車，駕六馬。

translations.literal: He further built a golden-root carriage drawn by six horses.
translations.idiomatic: He commissioned the six-horse golden state coach.

sentences.zh: 是月，玄臨聽訟觀閱囚徒，罪無輕重，多被原放。

translations.literal: That month Xuan attended the prison-review terrace and inspected convicts; regardless of light or heavy guilt most were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: That month he staged a jail review and freed prisoners wholesale.

sentences.zh: 有幹輿乞者，時或恤之。

translations.literal: Some pole-cart beggars he occasionally pitied.
translations.idiomatic: Even beggars sometimes received his petty charity.

sentences.zh: 其好行小惠如此。

translations.literal: His delight in petty favors was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his taste for small benevolences.

sentences.zh: 自以水德，壬辰，臘于祖。

translations.literal: Considering himself of water virtue, on renchen day he held year-end sacrifice at the ancestral shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Claiming water-phase cosmology he observed la rites at the imperial shrine.

sentences.zh: 改尚書都官郎為賊曹，又增置五校、三將及強弩、積射武衛官。

translations.literal: He renamed Bureau of Capital Affairs clerk to "Bandit Bureau"; further added five camps, three commands, and crossbow, volley, and palace guard posts.
translations.idiomatic: Renamed ministries for "bandits" and bloated palace armies.

sentences.zh: 元興三年，玄之永始二年也，尚書答「春蒐」字誤為「春菟」，凡所關署皆被降黜。

translations.literal: The third year of Yuanxing—his Yongshi second year—the Secretariat answered "spring hunt" character wrongly as "spring rabbit"; everyone whose documents bore it was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: A Secretariat typo—"spring hunt" written "spring hare"—triggered mass demotions.

sentences.zh: 玄大綱不理，而糾摘纖微，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Xuan ignored great governance yet picked at minute faults—all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: He neglected policy yet punished trivia.

sentences.zh: 以其妻劉氏為皇后，將修殿宇，乃移入東宮。

translations.literal: He took his wife Lady Liu as empress; about to renovate halls he moved into the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Naming Lady Liu empress, he seized the heir's Eastern Palace quarters.

sentences.zh: 又開東掖、平昌、廣莫及宮殿諸門，皆為三道。

translations.literal: He further opened Eastern Wing, Pingchang, Guangmo and many palace gates—each became triple passages.
translations.idiomatic: Palace gates were carved into triple avenues.

sentences.zh: 更造大輦，容三千人坐，以二百人舁之。

translations.literal: He built a giant palanquin seating three thousand attendants carried by two hundred bearers.
translations.idiomatic: A litter designed for three thousand sitters required two hundred porters.

sentences.zh: 性好畋遊，以體大不堪乘馬，又作徘徊輿，施轉關，令回動無滯。

translations.literal: By nature he loved hunting excursions; his frame could not bear horseback—so he built a "wavering litter" with rotating pivots so it could sway without sticking.
translations.idiomatic: Too heavy to ride, he invented a swiveling hunting sedan.

sentences.zh: 既不追尊祖曾，疑其禮義，問於群臣。

translations.literal: Neither posthumously honoring great-great-grandfather nor resolving ritual propriety, he questioned ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Unsettled on ancestral temples, he polled the court.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍徐廣據晉典宜追立七廟，又敬其父則子悅，位彌高者情理得申，道愈廣者納敬必普也。

translations.literal: Senior attendant Xu Guang cited Jin precedent that seven temples should be raised and that honoring the father pleases the son—the higher the station the clearer the principle, the broader the way the wider the homage.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guang urged seven shrines per Jin canon—revere fathers to delight sons.

sentences.zh: 玄曰：「《禮》雲三昭、三穆，與太祖為七，然則太祖必居廟之主也，昭穆皆自下之稱，則非逆數可知也。

translations.literal: Xuan said: "The Rites speak of three zhao, three mu—together with the Grand Progenitor they make seven—therefore the Grand Progenitor must be chief of the temple; zhao and mu are names applied from below—not inverse reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan argued ritual zhao-mu ordering places founding ancestor at axis.

sentences.zh: 禮，太祖東向，左昭右穆。

translations.literal: By rite the Grand Progenitor faces east; zhao left, mu right.
translations.idiomatic: Canonical layout faces the founder east with zhao and mu flanks.

sentences.zh: 如晉室之廟，則宣帝在昭穆之列，不得在太祖之位。

translations.literal: In Jin shrines Emperor Xuan stands within zhao-mu ranks—he cannot occupy Grand Progenitor's seat.
translations.idiomatic: Jin already installs Emperor Xuan in zhao-mu rows—not central ancestor.

sentences.zh: 昭穆既錯，太祖無寄，失之遠矣。

translations.literal: With zhao-mu already confused the Grand Progenitor has nowhere to lodge—the error runs deep.
translations.idiomatic: Misaligned ranks leave no seat for the primal ancestor.

sentences.zh: 」玄曾祖以上名位不顯，故不欲序列，且以王莽九廟見譏于前史，遂以一廟矯之，郊廟齋二日而已。

translations.literal: "Xuan's great-great-grandfather upward lacked illustrious names—he therefore declined ordering them; moreover Wang Mang's nine temples were mocked in earlier histories—so he falsified a single temple; suburban and temple fasts lasted but two days.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed of obscure forebears and dodging Wang Mang's nine-temple ridicule, he recognized only one shrine with minimal fasting.

sentences.zh: 秘書監卞承之曰：「祭不及祖，知楚德之不長也。

translations.literal: Secretariat overseer Bian Chengzhi said: "Sacrifice not reaching ancestors shows Chu virtue will not last."
translations.idiomatic: Bian Chengzhi quipped: neglecting ancestors doomed Chu.

sentences.zh: 」又毀晉小廟以廣台榭。

translations.literal: He further demolished minor Jin shrines to broaden terraces and pavilions.
translations.idiomatic: He tore down auxiliary Jin temples for pleasure buildings.

sentences.zh: 其庶母蒸嘗，靡有定所，忌日見賓客遊宴，唯至亡時一哭而已。

translations.literal: As for his concubine mother's seasonal offerings there was no fixed site; on taboo days he still received guests for outings and revelry—only at death hour did he weep once.
translations.idiomatic: Concubine mother's rites lacked stable altars; taboo anniversaries meant parties save one token wail.

sentences.zh: 期服之內，不廢音樂。

translations.literal: Within mourning months he did not cease music.
translations.idiomatic: Even in mourning white he kept musicians playing.

sentences.zh: 玄出遊水門，飄風飛其儀蓋。

translations.literal: When Xuan went out to Water Gate a whirlwind carried off his ceremonial canopy.
translations.idiomatic: A gust stripped his canopy at Water Gate.

sentences.zh: 夜，濤水入石頭，大桁流壞，殺人甚多。

translations.literal: At night tidal bore swept Stone Wall—great pontoon bridges broke—many died.
translations.idiomatic: Night tide smashed Stone fortress bridges and drowned crowds.

sentences.zh: 大風吹硃雀門樓，上層墜地。

translations.literal: Great wind struck Zhuque Gate tower—the upper story crashed to earth.
translations.idiomatic: Gales toppled the Zhuque Gate upper floor.

sentences.zh: 玄自篡盜之後，驕奢荒侈，遊獵無度，以夜繼晝。

translations.literal: After Xuan's usurpation theft he grew arrogant, extravagant, hunted without limit, continuing nights into days.
translations.idiomatic: Post-usurpation he reveled, hunted day and night.

sentences.zh: 兄偉葬日，旦哭晚遊，或一日之中屢出馳騁。

translations.literal: On brother Wei's burial day he wept at dawn yet rode out by evening—sometimes galloping several sorties in one day.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's funeral morning brought tears, evening brought hunts.

sentences.zh: 性又急暴，呼召嚴速，直官咸系馬省前，禁內嘩雜，無復朝廷之體。

translations.literal: His nature was also sudden and violent; summons came harsh and fast—duty officers all tethered horses before the ministry; inside the forbidden precincts noisy chaos replaced court dignity.
translations.idiomatic: Temper tantrums filled the palace yard with tethered horses and chaos.

sentences.zh: 於是百姓疲苦，朝野勞瘁，怨怒思亂者十室八九焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon common people wore out; court and countryside labored—nine houses in ten nursed resentment and plotted turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Exhaustion and hatred gripped nine households in ten.

sentences.zh: 於是劉裕、劉毅、何無忌等共謀興復。

translations.literal: Thereupon Liu Yu, Liu Yi, He Wuji and others plotted restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu, Liu Yi, and He Wuji conspired revival.

sentences.zh: 裕等斬桓脩於京口，斬桓弘於廣陵，河內太守辛扈興、弘農太守王元德、振威將軍童厚之、竟陵太守劉邁謀為內應。

translations.literal: Yu and party executed Huan Xiu at Jingkou and Huan Hong at Guangling; Prefect of Hanoi Xin Huxing, Prefect of Hongnong Wang Yuande, General Who Inspires Awe Tong Houzhi, Prefect of Jingling Liu Mai plotted inner collaboration.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu slew Huan Xiu and Hong while Xin Huxing, Wang Yuande, Tong Houzhi, Liu Mai promised interior aid.

sentences.zh: 至期，裕遣周安穆報之，而邁惶遽，遂以告玄。

translations.literal: When the hour came Yu sent Zhou Anmu to inform them, but Mai panicked and informed Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Anmu carried word; Liu Mai betrayed the plot to Xuan.

sentences.zh: 玄震駭，即殺扈興等，安穆馳去得免。

translations.literal: Xuan was shaken and immediately killed Huxing and others; Anmu galloped away and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan slaughtered conspirators while Zhou Anmu fled.

sentences.zh: 封邁重安侯，一宿又殺之。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed Mai as Marquis of Chong'an—after one night killed him too.
translations.idiomatic: He briefly titled Liu Mai marquis then murdered him overnight.

sentences.zh: 裕率義軍至竹裏，玄移還上宮，百僚步從，召侍官皆入止省中。

translations.literal: Yu led loyal troops to Zhuli; Xuan moved back to the upper palace—hundred officials followed on foot and summoned attendants into palace offices.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu advanced on Zhuli; Xuan retreated to the high palace with ministers afoot.

sentences.zh: 赦揚、豫、徐、兗、青、冀六州，加桓謙征討都督、假節，以殷仲文代桓脩，遣頓丘太守吳甫之、右衛將軍皇甫敷北距義軍。

translations.literal: He amnestied Yang, Yu, Xu, Yan, Qing, Ji six prefectures; named Huan Qian expedition commander-in-chief with credential authority; Yin Zhongwen replaced Huan Xiu; sent Dunqiu prefect Wu Fuzhi and Guards general Huangfu Fu north to block loyal forces.
translations.idiomatic: He issued hollow amnesty, gave Qian command against Liu Yu, replaced Xiu with Zhongwen, sent Wu Fuzhi and Huangfu Fu north.

sentences.zh: 裕等於江乘與戰，臨陣斬甫之，進至羅落橋，與敷戰，復梟其首。

translations.literal: Yu and others fought at Jiangcheng—beheaded Fuzhi on the field; advanced to Luoluo Bridge—fought Fu again and displayed his head.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangcheng Liu Yu killed Wu Fuzhi; at Luoluo Bridge slew Huangfu Fu.

sentences.zh: 玄聞之大懼，乃召諸道術人推算數為厭勝之法，乃問眾曰：「朕其敗乎？

translations.literal: When Xuan heard he was greatly afraid; he summoned Daoist augurs to calculate numerology for apotropaic magic; he asked the assembly: "Shall I be defeated?"
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Xuan consulted sorcerers and asked ministers if ruin loomed.

sentences.zh: 」曹靖之對曰：「神怒人怨，臣實懼焉。

translations.literal: Cao Jingzhi replied: "The gods are angry and men resentful—I truly fear."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jingzhi said gods and people alike despised him.

sentences.zh: 」玄曰：「人或可怨，神何為怒？

translations.literal: Xuan said: "Men may resent—why would gods rage?"
translations.idiomatic: Xuan asked why heaven would bother.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「移晉宗廟，飄泊失所，大楚之祭，不及于祖，此其所以怒也。

translations.literal: The reply: "You moved the Jin ancestral tablets wandering homeless; great Chu sacrifice does not reach ancestors—this is why they rage."
translations.idiomatic: Answer: relocating Jin shrines and omitting Chu founder rites angered heaven.

sentences.zh: 」玄曰：「卿何不諫？

translations.literal: Xuan said: "Why did you not remonstrate?"
translations.idiomatic: Xuan demanded why none warned him.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「輦上諸君子皆以為堯舜之世，臣何敢言！

translations.literal: The reply: "Those gentlemen on the palanquin all thought it Yao-Shun's age—how dare I speak!"
translations.idiomatic: Answer: courtiers pretended a golden age—who dared speak?

sentences.zh: 」玄愈忿懼，使桓謙、何澹之屯東陵，卞範之屯覆舟山西，眾合二萬，以距義軍。

translations.literal: Xuan grew angrier and more afraid; he sent Huan Qian and He Danzhi to encamp at East Mound, Bian Fanzhi west of Fuzhou Mountain—twenty thousand total—to resist loyal troops.
translations.idiomatic: He deployed Qian, Danzhi, and Fanzhi with twenty thousand against Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 裕至蔣山，使羸弱貫油帔登山，分張旗幟，數道並前。

translations.literal: When Yu reached Jiangshan he sent weak troops in oiled cloaks up the hill, spread banners wide, advancing on many tracks.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu feigned weakness—oiled cloaks on Jiangshan slopes and banners everywhere.

sentences.zh: 玄偵侯還云：「裕軍四塞，不知多少。

translations.literal: Xuan's scouts returned saying: "Yu armies fill four sides—I cannot know how many."
translations.idiomatic: Scouts reported Liu Yu surrounding them—numbers unknown.

sentences.zh: 」玄益憂惶，遣武衛將軍庾頤之配以精卒，副援諸軍。

translations.literal: Xuan grew more anxious; he assigned Guards general Yu Yizhi picked elite troops to reinforce all columns.
translations.idiomatic: He threw Yu Yizhi's crack troops into the line.

sentences.zh: 于時東北風急，義軍放火，煙塵張天，鼓噪之音震駭京邑。

translations.literal: At that moment northeast wind blew fierce; loyal troops kindled fire—smoke filled heaven; drum and shout shook the capital.
translations.idiomatic: A northeast gale fed Liu Yu's fires—smoke blotted the sky over Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 劉裕執鉞麾而進，謙等諸軍一時奔潰。

translations.literal: Liu Yu grasped axe-banner and advanced; Qian's army collapsed at once.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu waved his broadaxe; Qian's lines shattered.

sentences.zh: 玄率親信數千人聲言赴戰，遂將其子升、兄子浚出南掖門，西至石頭，使殷仲文具船，相與南奔。

translations.literal: Xuan led several thousand trusted followers claiming to join battle—then took his son Sheng and nephew Jun out the southern wing gate west to Stone Wall, ordered Yin Zhongwen to prepare boats, and fled south together.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan pretended to fight but slipped out Nanxu Gate toward Stone fortress with Sheng and Jun, Zhongwen arranging boats for escape.

sentences.zh: 初，玄在姑孰，將相星屢有變；

translations.literal: At first when Xuan was at Gushu minister and star omens changed repeatedly;
translations.idiomatic: At Gushu court stars had foretold trouble;

sentences.zh: 篡位之夕，月及太白，又入羽林，玄甚惡之。

translations.literal: the night of usurpation moon and Venus entered the Feathered Forest guard—Xuan greatly hated it.
translations.idiomatic: usurpation eve moon and Venus invaded the imperial guard asterism—ominous.

sentences.zh: 及敗走，腹心勸其戰，玄不暇答，直以策指天。

translations.literal: When fleeing, intimates urged battle—Xuan had no leisure to answer—only pointed his whip at heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Retreat advisors begged him to fight; he merely pointed his riding crop skyward.

sentences.zh: 而經日不得食，左右進以粗飯，咽不能下。

translations.literal: For whole days he could not eat; attendants offered coarse rice—he could not swallow.
translations.idiomatic: He starved, choking on coarse rice.

sentences.zh: 升時年數歲，抱玄胸而撫之，玄悲不自勝。

translations.literal: Sheng was then only a few years old—clasping Xuan's chest and stroking him—Xuan could not contain grief.
translations.idiomatic: Young Sheng hugged him as he sobbed.

sentences.zh: 劉裕以武陵王遵攝萬機，立行台，總百官。

translations.literal: Liu Yu installed Prince Zun of Wuling to handle myriad affairs, erecting field headquarters summoning hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu set Prince Zun as regent with mobile headquarters.

sentences.zh: 遣劉毅、劉道規躡玄，誅玄諸兄子及石康兄權、振兄洪等。

translations.literal: He sent Liu Yi and Liu Daogui to trail Xuan, executing Xuan's nephews and Shikang's brothers Quan, Zhen's brother Hong, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi hunted Xuan's kin—executing nephews and Huan Zhen's circle.

sentences.zh: 玄至尋陽，江州刺史郭昶之給其器用兵力。

translations.literal: When Xuan reached Xunyang, Inspector of Jiangzhou Guo Changzhi supplied equipment and troops.
translations.idiomatic: At Xunyang Guo Changzhi armed him.

sentences.zh: 殷仲文自後至，望見玄舟，旌旗輿服備帝者之儀，歎息曰：「敗中復振，故可也。

translations.literal: Yin Zhongwen arrived afterward—seeing Xuan's boats still bore imperial pennants and equipage—sighed: "To revive from defeat—acceptable indeed."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen mocked the imperial display amid flight.

sentences.zh: 」玄於是逼乘輿西上。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xuan forced the imperial carriage west.
translations.idiomatic: He compelled the emperor's train westward.

sentences.zh: 桓歆聚党向曆陽，宣城內史諸葛長民擊破之。

translations.literal: Huan Xin gathered faction toward Liyang—Interior Prefect of Xuancheng Zhuge Changmin crushed him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xin's march on Liyang failed before Zhuge Changmin.

sentences.zh: 玄於道作起居注，敘其距義軍之事，自謂經略指授，算無遺策，諸將違節度，以致虧喪，非戰之罪。

translations.literal: On the road Xuan composed a court diary narrating resistance to loyal troops—claiming strategy flawless and direction complete—generals disobeyed discipline causing defeat—not battle's fault.
translations.idiomatic: En route he penned a diary blaming generals for ruining his perfect plans.

sentences.zh: 於是不遑與群下謀議，唯耽思誦述，宣示遠近。

translations.literal: Therefore he had no leisure to consult groups below—only addicted himself to recitation and composition, proclaiming them far and near.
translations.idiomatic: Too rattled for council he drowned in rewriting edicts and broadcasting them everywhere.

sentences.zh: 玄至江陵，石康納之，張幔屋于城南，署置百官，以卞范之為尚書僕射，其餘職多用輕資。

translations.literal: When Xuan reached Jiangling Shikang welcomed him; he draped tent halls south of the city, installed hundred offices, named Bian Fanzhi Junior Mentor—most posts went to men of slight pedigree.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangling Huan Shikang hosted him; Xuan pitched imperial tents, staffed a shadow court with Fanzhi as vice-president and lightweight placemen elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 於是大修舟師，曾未三旬，眾且二萬，樓船器械甚盛。

translations.literal: Thereupon he greatly drilled naval forces—in less than thirty days followers approached twenty thousand; tower ships and gear flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he massed nearly twenty thousand sailors with formidable fleet trains.

sentences.zh: 謂其群黨曰：「卿等並清塗翼從朕躬，都下竊位者方應謝罪軍門，其觀卿等入石頭，無異雲霄中人也。」

translations.literal: He told his clique: "You all mount pure roads winging my person—those who stole posts below should soon beg forgiveness at army gates—watching you enter Stone Wall will be like watching men amid clouds."
translations.idiomatic: He boasted his allies would march Jiankang while usurpers groveled outside camp.

sentences.zh: 玄以奔敗之後，懼法令不肅，遂輕怒妄殺，人多離怨。

translations.literal: After flight and defeat Xuan feared laws lacked sternness—therefore lightly raged and killed recklessly—many drifted into resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Paranoia after rout bred arbitrary executions.

sentences.zh: 殷仲文諫曰：「陛下少播英譽，遠近所服，遂掃平荊雍，一匡京室，聲被八荒矣。

translations.literal: Yin Zhongwen remonstrated: "Your Majesty from youth spread splendid fame—which far and near obeyed—you then swept Jing–Yong and rectified the capital—your voice carried beyond eight wastes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen pleaded that Xuan once commanded reverence and restored Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 既據有極位，而遇此圮運，非為威不足也。

translations.literal: Already occupying the summit rank yet encountering this overturned fortune—is not because awe insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Misfortune stemmed not from weak awe.

sentences.zh: 百姓喁喁，想望皇澤，宜弘仁風，以收物情。

translations.literal: The hundred surnames murmur—they desire imperial grace—you should extend humane breeze to capture sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: People still hungered for mercy—policy should soften hearts.

sentences.zh: 」玄怒曰：「漢高、魏武幾遇敗，但諸將失利耳！

translations.literal: "Xuan angrily said: "Han Gaozu and Wei Wu encountered defeat several times—only generals lost battles!
translations.idiomatic: "He snapped that Liu Bang and Cao Cao lost battles yet endured.

sentences.zh: 以天文惡，故還都舊楚，而群小愚惑，妄生是非，方當糾之以猛，未宜施之以恩也。

translations.literal: Because celestial signs were ill we returned capital to old Chu—yet petty men foolishly stir right and wrong—we should discipline with severity—not yet apply kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Blaming astrology he insisted terror, not kindness, would tame rumor.

sentences.zh: 」玄左右稱玄為「桓詔」，桓胤諫曰：「詔者，施於辭令，不以為稱謂也。

translations.literal: "Xuan's intimates styled him "Huan Zhao"; Huan Yin remonstrated: "The word edict applies to orders—not as personal title.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers called him "Edict Huan"; Yin protested the misuse.

sentences.zh: 漢魏之主皆無此言，唯聞北虜以苻堅為'苻詔'耳。

translations.literal: Han–Wei lords never used this speech—I only hear northern barbarians called Fu Jian 'Fu Zhao.'"
translations.idiomatic: Only Former Qin jest titled Fu Jian "Edict Fu."

sentences.zh: 願陛下稽古帝則，令萬世可法。

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty examine antiquity's imperial norms—make myriad generations law.
translations.idiomatic: Yin begged him to model ancient kings.

sentences.zh: 」玄曰：「此事已行，今宣敕罷之，更為不祥。

translations.literal: "Xuan said: "This matter already proceeds—now proclaiming abolition would be even more ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan claimed stopping midstream augured worse luck.

sentences.zh: 必其宜革，可待事平也。

translations.literal: If truly appropriate to reform, await affairs settled.
translations.idiomatic: Change could wait until victory.

sentences.zh: 」荊州郡守以玄播越，或遣使通表，有匪寧之辭，玄悉不受，仍乃更令所在表賀遷都。

translations.literal: "Jingzhou prefects thought Xuan wandered homeless—some sent envoys with memorials containing unrest phrases—Xuan accepted none—instead ordered locales to memorialize congratulating capital relocation.
translations.idiomatic: Regional governors offered condolences for his exile; Xuan refused and forced congratulations on his "move."

sentences.zh: 玄遣遊擊將軍何澹之、武衛將軍庾稚祖、江夏太守桓道恭就郭銓以數千人守湓口。

translations.literal: Xuan sent Mobile Corps general He Danzhi, Guards general Yu Zhizu, and Jiangxia prefect Huan Daogong to Guo Quan with several thousand holding Penkou.
translations.idiomatic: He tasked Danzhi, Zhizu, Daogong under Guo Quan to defend Penkou.

sentences.zh: 又遣輔國將軍桓振往義陽聚眾，至弋陽，為龍驤將軍胡譁所破，振單騎走還。

translations.literal: He further sent General Who Assists the State Huan Zhen to gather crowds at Yiyang—reaching Yiyang he was broken by Dragon-General Hu Hua—Zhen fled alone back.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's levy at Yiyang collapsed before Hu Hua.

sentences.zh: 何無忌、劉道規等破郭銓、何澹之、郭昶之于桑落洲，進師尋陽。

translations.literal: He Wuji and Liu Daogui crushed Guo Quan, He Danzhi, Guo Changzhi at Sangluo Isle and advanced on Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal fleets routed Quan's coalition at Sangluo Isle then sailed toward Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 玄率舟艦二百發江陵，使苻宏、羊僧壽為前鋒。

translations.literal: Xuan led two hundred vessels from Jiangling and ordered Fu Hong and Yang Shoushou as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred war barges left Jiangling under Fu Hong and Shoushou.

sentences.zh: 以鄱陽太守徐放為散騎常侍，欲遣說解義軍，謂放曰：「諸人不識天命，致此妄作，遂懼禍屯結，不能自反。

translations.literal: He named Poyang prefect Xu Fang senior attendant—intending to send persuasion to loyal armies—telling Fang: "Those men do not know Heaven's mandate—causing this reckless action—they fear calamity knotted together—unable to reverse.
translations.idiomatic: He elevated Xu Fang to lobby Liu Yu's coalition.

sentences.zh: 卿三州所信，可明示朕心，若退軍散甲，當與之更始，各授位任，令不失分。

translations.literal: You whom three prefectures trust—can openly reveal my heart—if they withdraw troops and scatter armor I shall renew them together—each awarded rank—making none lose proper station.
translations.idiomatic: Fang promised reinstatement for rebels who disarmed.

sentences.zh: 江水在此，朕不食言。

translations.literal: The Yangzi waters stand here—I shall not break my word.
translations.idiomatic: "The river hears my oath—I keep faith."

sentences.zh: 」放對曰：「劉裕為唱端之主，劉毅兄為陛下所誅，並不可說也。

translations.literal: "Fang replied: "Liu Yu is the rebellion's chief—Liu Yi's elder brother was executed by Your Majesty—both cannot be persuaded.
translations.idiomatic: Fang countered that Liu Yu would never trust him after Liu Yi died.

sentences.zh: 輒當申聖旨于何無忌。

translations.literal: I shall relay Your Sagely intent to He Wuji.
translations.idiomatic: "I will convey your orders to He Wuji alone."

sentences.zh: 」玄曰：「卿使若有功，當以吳興相敘。

translations.literal: "Xuan said: "If your mission succeeds I shall appoint you Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan promised Wuxing prefecture for success.

sentences.zh: 」放遂受使，入無忌軍。

translations.literal: "Fang thereupon accepted mission and entered Wuji's army.
translations.idiomatic: Fang rode into Wuji's camp.

sentences.zh: 魏詠之破桓歆于曆陽，諸葛長民又敗歆於芍陂，歆單馬渡淮。

translations.literal: Wei Yongzhi crushed Huan Xin at Liyang; Zhuge Changmin again defeated Xin at Quebei—Xin crossed Huai alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Xin fled north across the Huai after twin defeats.

sentences.zh: 毅率道規及下邳太守孟懷玉與玄戰于崢嶸洲。

translations.literal: Yi led Daogui and Xiapi prefect Meng Huaiyu against Xuan at Zhengrong Isle.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi joined Daogui and Meng Huaiyu at Zhengrong sandbank.

sentences.zh: 于時義軍數千，玄兵甚盛，而玄懼有敗衄，常漾輕舸於舫側，故其眾莫有鬥心。

translations.literal: At the time loyal troops numbered only thousands—Xuan's forces were very strong—yet Xuan feared defeat—always anchored light skiffs beside his flagship—therefore his host lacked fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Though outnumbered, Liu Yu's men burned to fight; Xuan tethered escape boats and killed morale.

sentences.zh: 義軍乘風縱火，盡銳爭先，玄眾大潰，燒輜重夜遁，郭銓歸降。

translations.literal: Loyal armies rode the wind to loose fire—all vanguard vied to lead—Xuan's army routed utterly—burned baggage fled by night—Guo Quan surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Wind-fed fires shattered Xuan's fleet; Quan defected.

sentences.zh: 玄故將劉統、馮稚等聚黨四百人，襲破尋陽城，毅遣建威將軍劉懷肅討平之。

translations.literal: Xuan's former generals Liu Tong, Feng Zhi and others gathered four hundred raiders—stormed Xunyang city—Yi sent General Who Establishes Might Liu Huaisu to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits seized Xunyang until Liu Huaisu crushed them.

sentences.zh: 玄留永安皇后及皇后于巴陵。

translations.literal: Xuan detained Empress Yongan and the empress at Baling.
translations.idiomatic: He stranded both queens at Baling.

sentences.zh: 殷仲文時在玄艦，求出別船收集散軍，因叛玄，奉二後奔于夏口。

translations.literal: Yin Zhongwen was then aboard Xuan's ship—begged transfer to another vessel to gather scattered troops—thereupon rebelled against Xuan—escorting both queens fleeing toward Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen defected midstream and spirited the consorts to Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 玄入江陵城，馮該勸使更下戰，玄不從，欲出漢川，投梁州刺史桓希，而人情乖阻，制令不行。

translations.literal: Xuan entered Jiangling city—Feng Gai urged another descent to battle—Xuan refused—wished to exit Han river valleys toward Inspector of Liangzhou Huan Xi—but sentiment turned obstructive—commands failed.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangling refused another stand and hoped to reach Liangzhou via Han—but controls collapsed.

sentences.zh: 玄乘馬出城，至門，左右於暗中斫之，不中，前後相殺交橫，玄僅得至船。

translations.literal: Xuan rode horse out of city—reaching gate—followers hacked from shadows—missed—front and rear slew each other crisscross—barely reached boats.
translations.idiomatic: Ambush at the gate nearly killed him before he reached boats.

sentences.zh: 於是荊州別駕王康產奉帝入南郡府舍，太守王騰之率文武營衛。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jingzhou adjunct Wang Kangchan presented emperor into Nanjun headquarters—prefect Wang Tengzhi led civil and military guarding.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kangchan sheltered the emperor while Tengzhi mustered defense.

sentences.zh: 時益州刺史毛璩使其從孫祐之、參軍費恬送弟璠喪葬江陵，有眾二百，璩弟子脩之為玄屯騎校尉，誘玄以入蜀，玄從之。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yi prefecture Mao Fan dispatched grandnephew Youzhi and aide Fei Tian escorting younger brother Fan's funeral to Jiangling—two hundred troops following—younger clan disciple Xiuzhi served Xuan as Colonel of Camped Cavalry—enticed Xuan into Shu—Xuan followed.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Fan's kin feigned escorting a corpse convoy to lure Xuan west.

sentences.zh: 達枚回洲，恬與祐之迎擊玄，矢下如雨。

translations.literal: Reaching Meihui Isle Fei Tian with Youzhi ambushed Xuan—arrows fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: At Meihui Isle Mao loyalists raked him with arrows.

sentences.zh: 玄嬖人丁仙期、萬蓋等以身敝玄，並中數十箭而死。

translations.literal: Xuan's favorites Ding Xianqi, Wan Gai and others used bodies to shield Xuan—together struck by dozens of arrows and died.
translations.idiomatic: Catamites absorbed volleys for him.

sentences.zh: 玄被箭，其子升輒拔去之。

translations.literal: Struck by arrows—his son Sheng continually pulled them free.
translations.idiomatic: Boy Huan Sheng plucked shafts from his father's flesh.

sentences.zh: 益州督護馮遷抽刀而前，玄拔頭上玉導與之，仍曰：「是何人邪？

translations.literal: Yi Protectorate Feng Qian drew blade forward—Xuan pulled jade hairpin from head handing it—still said: "What person are you?
translations.idiomatic: Xuan offered his jade pin and whimpered.

sentences.zh: 敢殺天子！

translations.literal: "You dare kill Heaven's Son!
translations.idiomatic: "Who strikes the Son of Heaven?"

sentences.zh: 」遷曰：「欲殺天子之賊耳。

translations.literal: "Qian said: "One who kills the thief styling Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: "The man killing the counterfeit emperor," Feng replied.

sentences.zh: 」遂斬之，時年三十六。

translations.literal: Thereupon executed him—aged thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: They cut him down at thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 又斬石康及浚等五級，庾頤之戰死。

translations.literal: Also executed Shikang and Jun among five grades—Yu Yizhi died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Shikang and Jun died too; Yu Yizhi fell fighting.

sentences.zh: 升云：「我是豫章王，諸君勿見殺。

translations.literal: Sheng cried: "I am Prince of Yuzhang—you gentlemen must not kill me.
translations.idiomatic: Young Sheng begged for life as prince.

sentences.zh: 」送至江陵市斬之。

translations.literal: Delivered to Jiangling market executed.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers marched him to Jiangling and killed him.

sentences.zh: 初，玄在宮中，恆覺不安，若為鬼神所擾，語其所親云：「恐己當死，故與時競。

translations.literal: At first when Xuan dwelt in palace always felt uneasy—as if ghosts disturbed—told intimates: "I fear I shall die—therefore race time.
translations.idiomatic: He confessed dread that death chased him.

sentences.zh: 」元興中，衡陽有雌雞化為雄，八十日而冠萎。

translations.literal: During Yuanxing Hengyang hen transformed cock—eighty days then crown wilted.
translations.idiomatic: A hen crowed like rooster for eighty days—omens piled.

sentences.zh: 及玄建國于楚，衡陽屬焉，自篡盜至敗，時凡八旬矣。

translations.literal: When Xuan founded Chu state—Hengyang fell within—his rule lasted eighty days.
translations.idiomatic: From usurpation to ruin totaled eighty days.

sentences.zh: 其時有童謠云：「長幹巷，巷長幹，今年殺郎君，後年斬諸桓。

translations.literal: At the time a children's rhyme ran: "Long Dry Lane—lane long dry—this year kills the young lord—next year beheads all Huans."
translations.idiomatic: Street rhyme augured Yuanxian's death and clan wipeout.

sentences.zh: 」其凶兆符會如此。

translations.literal: Its evil omens matched thus.
translations.idiomatic: Omens lined up exactly.

sentences.zh: 郎君，謂元顯也。

translations.literal: Young lord meant Yuanxian.
translations.idiomatic: "Young lord" mocked Sima Yuanxian.

sentences.zh: 是月，王騰之奉帝入居太府。

translations.literal: That month Wang Tengzhi presented emperor lodging in Grand Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Tengzhi housed the emperor at the treasury compound.

sentences.zh: 桓謙亦聚眾沮中，為玄舉哀，立喪庭，偽諡為武悼皇帝。

translations.literal: Huan Qian likewise gathered crowds amid Ju marshes—mourning Xuan—establishing mourning hall—false posthumous title Martial-Mournful Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Qian staged funeral rites for Xuan as emperor.

sentences.zh: 毅等傳送玄首，梟於大桁，百姓觀者莫不欣幸。

translations.literal: Yi and others forwarded Xuan's head—displayed at great pontoon—spectators none who did not rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: They spiked Xuan's head on Jiankang bridge amid cheers.

sentences.zh: 何無忌等攻桓謙於馬頭，桓蔚于龍洲，皆破之。

translations.literal: He Wuji and party attacked Huan Qian at Matou—Huan Wei at Dragon Isle—both defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji shattered Qian at Matou and Wei on Dragon Isle.

sentences.zh: 義軍乘勝競進，振、該等距戰於靈溪，道規等敗績，死沒者千餘人。

translations.literal: Victorious loyal armies pressed ahead—Zhen, Gai resisted at Spirit Creek—Daogui's contingent routed—more than a thousand dead submerged.
translations.idiomatic: Assault on Lingxi ford bloodied Liu Yu's advance.

sentences.zh: 義軍退次尋陽，更繕舟甲。

translations.literal: Loyal armies withdrew to encamp Xunyang—refitting vessels and armor.
translations.idiomatic: They fell back to Xunyang to rebuild fleet.

sentences.zh: 毛璩自領梁州，遣將攻漢中，殺桓希。

translations.literal: Mao Fan personally commanded Liangzhou—sent generals attacking Hanzhong—slew Huan Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Fan seized Liangzhou and killed Xi in Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 江夏相張暢之、高平太守劉懷肅攻何澹之於西塞磯，破之。

translations.literal: Xiakai chief Zhang Changzhi and Gaoping prefect Liu Huaisu attacked He Danzhi at West Barrier Shoal—defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang and Huaisu smashed Danzhi's river pickets.

sentences.zh: 振遣桓蔚代王曠守襄陽。

translations.literal: Zhen dispatched Huan Wei replacing Wang Kuang guarding Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen posted Wei at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 道規進討武昌，破偽太守王旻。

translations.literal: Daogui advanced on Wuchang—defeated bogus prefect Wang Min.
translations.idiomatic: Daogui took Wuchang from Wang Min.

sentences.zh: 魏詠之、劉籓破桓石綏于白茅。

translations.literal: Wei Yongzhi and Liu Fan crushed Huan Shisui at White Reed.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi beat Shisui at White Reed marsh.

sentences.zh: 義軍發尋陽。

translations.literal: Loyal armies sailed from Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: The loyal fleet weighed anchor at Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 桓亮自號江州刺史，侵豫章，江州刺史劉敬宣討走之。

translations.literal: Huan Liang styled himself Inspector of Jiangzhou—invaded Yuzhang—Inspector Liu Jingxuan drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's Jiangzhou bid collapsed before Jingxuan.

sentences.zh: 義軍進次夏口。

translations.literal: Victorious armies advanced encamping Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Columns closed on Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 偽鎮東將軍馮該等守夏口，揚武將軍孟山圖據魯城，輔國將軍桓山客守偃月壘。

translations.literal: Bogus General Who Guards East Feng Gai and others guarded Xiakou—General Who Inspires Might Meng Shantu held Lu fortress—General Who Assists the State Huan Shanke defended Crescent Rampart.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Gai barred Xiakou; Meng Shantu Lu city; Shanke crescent wall.

sentences.zh: 劉毅攻魯城，道規攻偃月壘，無忌與檀祗列艦中流，以防越逸。

translations.literal: Liu Yi assaulted Lu fortress—Daogui assaulted Crescent Rampart—Wuji with Tan Zhi chained ships midstream to block escape.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and Daogui stormed twin citadels while Wuji sealed the river.

sentences.zh: 義軍騰赴，叫聲動山谷，自辰及午，二城俱潰，馮該散走，生擒山客。

translations.literal: Loyal armies surged—shouts shook valleys—from chen hour to noon both fortresses fell—Feng Gai scattered fleeing—Shanke captured alive.
translations.idiomatic: Morning assault broke both forts; Shanke taken.

sentences.zh: 毅等平巴陵。

translations.literal: Yi and others pacified Baling.
translations.idiomatic: They cleared Baling.

sentences.zh: 毛璩遣涪陵太守文處茂東下，振遣桓放之為益州，屯夷陵，處茂距戰，放之敗走，還江陵。

translations.literal: Mao Fan sent Fuling prefect Wen Chuma east—Zhen dispatched Huan Fangzhi as Yi prefect encamping Yiling—Chuma resisted—Fangzhi fled back Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Flanking moves traded blows along the Yangzi corridor.

sentences.zh: 義熙元年正月，南陽太守魯宗之起義兵襲襄陽，破偽雍州刺史桓蔚。

translations.literal: First month Yixi first year—Nanyang prefect Lu Zongzhi raised loyal troops attacking Xiangyang—defeated bogus Yongzhou inspector Huan Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yixi 405 Lu Zongzhi routed Huan Wei at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 無忌諸軍次江陵之馬頭，振擁帝出營江津。

translations.literal: Wuji's columns halted south of Jiangling at Matou—Zhen forced emperor out to Jiang ford camp.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen marched the puppet emperor out to the Jiang ford camp.

sentences.zh: 魯宗之率眾於柞溪，破偽武賁中郎溫楷，進至紀南。

translations.literal: Lu Zongzhi led host at Zha creek—defeated bogus Tiger Guards colonel Wen Kai—advanced to Ji south.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhi smashed Wen Kai and pressed Ji city's southern flank.

sentences.zh: 振自擊宗之，宗之失利。

translations.literal: Zhen personally struck Zongzhi—Zongzhi lost.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen beat Zongzhi in the field.

sentences.zh: 時蜀軍據靈溪，毅率無忌、道規等破馮該軍，推鋒而前，即平江陵。

translations.literal: At that time Shu troops held Spirit Creek—Yi led Wuji and Daogui crushing Feng Gai's army—spearheading forward—thereupon pacifying Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi punched through Lingxi and retook Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 振見火起，知城已陷，乃與謙等北走。

translations.literal: Seeing fire rise—knowing city already fallen—Zhen with Qian fled north.
translations.idiomatic: Smoke told Zhen the city had fallen; he bolted with Qian.

sentences.zh: 是日，安帝反正。

translations.literal: That day Emperor An returned legitimate rule.
translations.idiomatic: The same day Emperor An was restored.

sentences.zh: 大赦天下，唯逆黨就戮，詔特免桓胤一人。

translations.literal: Great amnesty under Heaven—only traitor clans executed—edict specially spared Huan Yin alone.
translations.idiomatic: Amnesty everywhere save usurper families—only Yin pardoned.

sentences.zh: 桓亮自豫章，自號鎮南將軍、湘州刺史。

translations.literal: Huan Liang from Yuzhang styled himself General Who Guards South and Inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liang reasserted southern titles from Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 苻宏寇安成、廬陵，劉敬宣遣將討之，宏走入湘中。

translations.literal: Fu Hong raided Ancheng and Luling—Liu Jingxuan sent generals—Hong fled into Xiang midlands.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Hong skirmished south until Jingxuan chased him into the Xiang backcountry.

sentences.zh: 二月，桓謙、何澹之、溫楷等奔于姚興。

translations.literal: Second month Huan Qian, He Danzhi, Wen Kai fled to Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Qian, Danzhi, and Kai ran to Later Qin.

sentences.zh: 桓振與宏出自溳城，襲破江陵，劉懷肅自雲杜伐振等，破之。

translations.literal: Huan Zhen with Hong emerged from Yun fort—raided Jiangling—Liu Huaisu from Yundu campaigned Zhen and others—defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen and Hong retook Jiangling briefly until Huaisu repulsed them.

sentences.zh: 廣武將軍唐興斬振及偽輔國將軍桓珍，毅於臨鄣斬偽零陵太守劉叔祖。

translations.literal: General Who Calms Warfare Tang Xing beheaded Zhen and bogus General Who Assists the State Huan Zhen; Yi at Linzhang executed bogus Prefect of Lingling Liu Shuzu.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Xing killed Zhen; Liu Yi took Shuzu's head.

sentences.zh: 桓亮、苻宏復出冠湘中，害郡守長吏，檀祗討宏於湘東，斬之，廣武將軍郭彌斬亮于益陽，其餘擁眾假號皆討平之。

translations.literal: Huan Liang and Fu Hong again raided Xiang midlands—murdering prefects and magistrates—Tan Zhi campaigned Hong in eastern Xiang—killed him—General Who Calms Warfare Guo Mi killed Liang at Yiyang—remaining self-styled hosts were mopped up.
translations.idiomatic: Mopping up: Tan Zhi killed Hong; Guo Mi slew Liang; stragglers purged.

sentences.zh: 詔徙桓胤及諸党與于新安諸郡。

translations.literal: Edict exiled Huan Yin and clique to Xin'an commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Surviving Huan kin were banished to Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 三年，東陽太守殷仲文與永嘉太守駱球謀反，欲建桓胤為嗣，曹靖之、桓石鬆、卞承之、劉延祖等潛相交結，劉裕以次收斬之，並誅其家屬。

translations.literal: Three years later—Dongyang prefect Yin Zhongwen and Yongjia prefect Luo Qiu conspired revolt—wishing to enthrone Huan Yin—Cao Jingzhi, Huan Song, Bian Chengzhi, Liu Yanzu quietly linked—Liu Yu arrested and executed in order including families.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhongwen's 408 plot to restore Yin saw every accomplice exterminated.

sentences.zh: 後桓謙走入蜀，蜀賊譙縱以謙為荊州刺史，使率兵而下，荊楚之眾多應之。

translations.literal: Later Huan Qian fled into Shu—bandit Qiao Zong made Qian Jingzhou inspector—ordered southward campaign—Jing–Chu hosts largely answered.
translations.idiomatic: Qian served Qiao Zong's bid from Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 謙至枝江，荊州刺史劉道規斬之，梁州刺史傅歆又斬桓石綏，桓氏遂滅。

translations.literal: Qian reached Zhijiang—Jingzhou inspector Liu Daogui beheaded him—Liangzhou inspector Fu Xin also killed Huan Shisui—Huan clan thus extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Daogui and Fu Xin ended the Huan line.

sentences.zh: 卞范之

translations.literal: Rubric: Bian Fanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Subsection title: Bian Fanzhi.

sentences.zh: 卞范之字敬祖，濟陰宛句人也，識悟聰敏，見美於當世。

translations.literal: Bian Fanzhi, courtesy name Jingzu, a man of Wancun in Jiyin—perceptive, clever, praised by his age.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Fanzhi of Wancun was celebrated for quick wit.

sentences.zh: 太元中，自丹陽丞為始安太守。

translations.literal: During Taiyuan he went from Danyang aide to Shian prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan promotions took him from Danyang aide to Shian governor.

sentences.zh: 桓玄少與之游，及玄為江州，引為長史，委以心膂之任，潛謀密計，莫不決之。

translations.literal: In youth Huan Xuan roamed with him; when Xuan held Jiangzhou he drew him as chief clerk—entrusted heart-and-back duties—secret plots—none decided without him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan trusted Fanzhi with every conspiracy once Jiangzhou fell to him.

sentences.zh: 後玄將為篡亂，以範之為丹陽尹。

translations.literal: Later when Xuan would usurp—named Fanzhi prefect of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: As coup neared Xuan installed him at Danyang.

sentences.zh: 范之與殷仲文陰撰策命，進範之為征虜將軍、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Fanzhi with Yin Zhongwen secretly drafted abdication edicts—advanced Fanzhi to General Who Punishes the Barbarians and senior attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He and Zhongwen forged abdication scripts and seized generalships.

sentences.zh: 玄僭位，以範之為侍中，班劍二十人，進號後將軍，封臨汝縣公。

translations.literal: When Xuan usurped—named Fanzhi Palace Attendant with twenty sword attendants—advanced title Rear General—enfeoffed Duke of Linru county.
translations.idiomatic: Usurpation won Fanzhi palace rank and Linru dukedom.

sentences.zh: 其禪詔，即范之文也。

translations.literal: The abdication edicts were Fanzhi's prose.
translations.idiomatic: His pen authored every abdication document.

sentences.zh: 玄既奢侈無度，范之亦盛營館第。

translations.literal: Once Xuan grew extravagant beyond measure—Fanzhi likewise built mansions vast.
translations.idiomatic: As Xuan spent recklessly Fanzhi threw up rival estates.

sentences.zh: 自以佐命元勳，深懷矜伐，以富貴驕人，子弟慠慢，眾咸畏嫉之。

translations.literal: Deeming himself meritorious minister of Mandate, he deeply harbored self-pride—flaunting wealth and rank—sons and younger kin arrogant; all feared and resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Fanzhi preened as founding hero; his brash kin earned universal loathing.

sentences.zh: 義軍起，范之屯兵於覆舟山西，為劉毅所敗，隨玄西走，玄又以范之為尚書僕射。

translations.literal: When loyal troops rose Fanzhi encamped west of Fuzhou Mountain—defeated by Liu Yi—followed Xuan west; Xuan again made Fanzhi Junior Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi routed Fanzhi at Fuzhou; Fanzhi fled with Xuan and regained vice presidency.

sentences.zh: 玄為劉毅等所敗，左右分散，唯範之在側。

translations.literal: When Xuan was defeated by Liu Yi and company—followers scattered—only Fanzhi remained at his side.
translations.idiomatic: At the rout only Bian Fanzhi stayed with Xuan.

sentences.zh: 玄平，斬於江陵。

translations.literal: After Xuan's pacification [Fanzhi] was beheaded at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: With Xuan gone Fanzhi lost his head at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 殷仲文

translations.literal: Section heading: Yin Zhongwen.
translations.idiomatic: Subsection title: Yin Zhongwen.

sentences.zh: 殷仲文，南蠻校尉覬之弟也。

translations.literal: Yin Zhongwen—younger brother of Colonel of Southern Man Yin Jizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen was Yin Jizhi's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 少有才藻，美容貌。

translations.literal: In youth he possessed literary talent and handsome features.
translations.idiomatic: Young Zhongwen wrote well and looked striking.

sentences.zh: 從兄仲堪薦之于會稽王道子，即引為驃騎參軍，甚相賞待。

translations.literal: Elder cousin Zhongkan recommended him to Prince of Kuaiji Wang Daozi—who immediately drew him as aide to Cavalry General—greatly appreciating him.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhongkan introduced him to Prince Daozi as adjutant-cavalry.

sentences.zh: 俄轉諮議參軍，後為元顯征虜長史。

translations.literal: Soon transferred advisory aide—later Yuanxian's chief clerk under General Who Punishes Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to advisory aide then Yuanxian's secretary.

sentences.zh: 會桓玄與朝廷有隙，玄之姊，仲文之妻，疑而間之，左遷新安太守。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan fell out with court—Xuan's elder sister being Zhongwen's wife—suspicion estranged him—demoted to prefect of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Kinship to Xuan cost him Xin'an exile.

sentences.zh: 仲文于玄雖為姻親，而素不交密，及聞玄平京師，便棄郡投焉。

translations.literal: Though Zhongwen was Xuan's affinal kin—normally not intimate—upon hearing Xuan took Jiankang he abandoned his command and fled to him.
translations.idiomatic: He betrayed Xin'an to join Xuan's coup.

sentences.zh: 玄甚悅之，以為諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Xuan greatly delighted—named him advisory aide.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan welcomed him as strategist.

sentences.zh: 時王謐見禮而不親，卞範之被親而少禮，而寵遇隆重，兼于王、卞矣。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Mi received ritual courtesy without intimacy; Bian Fanzhi intimate yet lacking ritual—while Zhongwen's favor outstripped both Wang and Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen outranked Wang Mi and Fanzhi in Xuan's esteem.

sentences.zh: 玄將為亂，使總領詔命，以為侍中，領左衛將軍。

translations.literal: When Xuan would rebel—assigned general supervision of edicts—named Palace Attendant with Guards of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted Xuan's palace orders and commanded imperial guards.

sentences.zh: 玄九錫，仲文之辭也。

translations.literal: Xuan's nine-bestowal rhetoric—Zhongwen's phrases.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen penned the nine insignia memorial.

sentences.zh: 初，玄篡位入宮，其床忽陷，群下失色，仲文曰：「將由聖德深厚，地不能載。

translations.literal: At first when Xuan usurped entering palace—the bed suddenly sank—assembly lost color—Zhongwen said: "Surely because sagely virtue runs deep—earth cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan's throne collapsed through the floor Zhongwen spun it as virtue too heavy for soil.

sentences.zh: 」玄大悅。

translations.literal: "Xuan greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan glowed at the flattery.

sentences.zh: 」以佐命親貴，厚自封崇，輿馬器服，窮極綺麗，後房伎妾數十，絲竹不絕音。

translations.literal: "Because Mandate merit intimate noble—generously aggrandized himself—carriages horses utensils garments utterly sumptuous—rear chambers dozens of singing girls—strings and winds never silent.
translations.idiomatic: He looted titles, stacked concubines, and dressed like an emperor.

sentences.zh: 性貪吝，多納貨賄，家累千金，常若不足。

translations.literal: By nature greedy and stingy—received many bribes—household piled thousand gold—always seeming insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: He hoarded bribes yet never felt rich.

sentences.zh: 玄為劉裕所敗，隨玄西走，其珍寶玩好悉藏地中，皆變為土。

translations.literal: When Xuan was defeated by Liu Yu—following Xuan west—his treasures and curiosities were all buried underground—they turned to dirt.
translations.idiomatic: Buried loot dissolved to mud on his flight.

sentences.zh: 至巴陵，因奉二後投義軍，而為鎮軍長史，轉尚書。

translations.literal: Reaching Baling—thereupon delivered both queens submitting to loyal armies—became chief clerk to Army Who Guards the Army—later Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: At Baling he defected with consorts and Liu Yu named him secretary.

sentences.zh: 帝初反正，抗表自解曰：「臣聞洪波振壑，川無恬鱗；

translations.literal: When emperor first restored legitimacy—Zhongwen submitted memorial refusing office saying: "I have heard great waves shake ravines—rivers hold no tranquil scales;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized self-indictment with classical metaphors.

sentences.zh: 驚飆拂野，林無靜柯。

translations.literal: Gale sweeps wilds—forests hold no quiet branches.
translations.idiomatic: Storms leave no calm branches.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why so?

sentences.zh: 勢弱則受制於巨力，質微則無以自保。

translations.literal: Weak momentum then controlled by mighty force—feeble substance then nothing to protect itself.
translations.idiomatic: Weak things fall prey to power.

sentences.zh: 於理雖可得而言，於臣實非所敢譬。

translations.literal: Though principle permits speech—in my case truly no apt comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Theory fits others—not his cowardice.

sentences.zh: 昔桓玄之代，誠復驅逼者眾。

translations.literal: In Huan Xuan's usurpation indeed many were driven and threatened.
translations.idiomatic: Usurpation press-ganged many.

sentences.zh: 至如微臣，罪實深矣，進不能見危授命，亡身殉國；

translations.literal: As for petty minister—guilt runs truly deep—advancing could not hand life amid peril—die body for state;
translations.idiomatic: He confessed failing to martyr himself for Jin.

sentences.zh: 退不能辭粟首陽，拂衣高謝。

translations.literal: retreating could not refuse grain at Shouyang—brush cloak and retire high.
translations.idiomatic: Nor did he starve on Shouyang like worthy recluses.

sentences.zh: 遂乃宴安昏寵，叨昧偽封，錫文篡事，曾無獨固。

translations.literal: Yet settled in reckless favor—shamelessly accepting false enfeoffment—copper-and-bamboo usurpation texts—never independently resisted.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted Xuan's puppet offices without protest.

sentences.zh: 名義以之俱淪，情節自茲兼撓，宜其極法，以判忠邪。

translations.literal: Reputation and duty together sank—sentiment and principle both compromised—should receive utmost law—to distinguish loyal from wicked.
translations.idiomatic: He deserved execution for moral collapse.

sentences.zh: 會鎮軍將軍劉裕匡復社稷，大弘善貸，佇一戮於微命，申三驅於大信，既惠之以首領，又申之以縶維。

translations.literal: When General Who Guards the Army Liu Yu restored altars—greatly extending kindness—awaiting single execution of petty life—extending three-hunt faith—already sparing heads—again binding with reins.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Liu Yu spared him despite guilt.

sentences.zh: 于時皇輿否隔，天人未泰，用忘進退，是以僶俯從事，自同令人。

translations.literal: At that time imperial carriage obstructed—Heaven and men not tranquil—forgetting advance and retreat—therefore stooped to serve—equating myself with vulgar persons.
translations.idiomatic: Anarchy forced him to collaborate.

sentences.zh: 今宸極反正，唯新告始，憲章既明，品物思舊，臣亦胡顏之厚，可以顯居榮次！

translations.literal: Now polar throne restored—renewal proclaimed—statutes clarified—things recall former virtue—how thick-faced dare I occupy glorious rank!
translations.idiomatic: Restoration exposed his shame.

sentences.zh: 乞解所職，待罪私門。

translations.literal: Begging dismissal from offices—awaiting punishment at private gate.
translations.idiomatic: He begged demotion and house arrest.

sentences.zh: 違離闕庭，乃心慕戀。

translations.literal: Departing palace gates—heart nonetheless yearns.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed nostalgia for court despite resignation.

sentences.zh: 」詔不許。

translations.literal: "Edict refused.
translations.idiomatic: Throne refused his resignation.

sentences.zh: 仲文因月朔與眾至大司馬府，府中有老槐樹，顧之良久而歎曰：「此樹婆娑，無復生意！

translations.literal: Zhongwen therefore on new-moon assembly with crowd reached Grand Marshal mansion—mansion contained ancient locust tree—gazing long sighed: "This tree dances gracefully—no longer bears life!
translations.idiomatic: Before Liu Yu's locust he mourned his career.

sentences.zh: 」仲文素有名望，自謂必當朝政，又謝混之徒疇昔所輕者，並皆比肩，常怏怏不得志。

translations.literal: "Zhongwen always possessed fame—self-thinking surely would handle court governance—yet men like Xie Hun once belittled—now stood shoulder to shoulder—normally resentful unfulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Peers he once snubbed now outranked him.

sentences.zh: 忽遷為東陽太守，意彌不平。

translations.literal: Suddenly transferred Dongyang prefect—mood still more unequal.
translations.idiomatic: Demotion to Dongyang embittered him.

sentences.zh: 劉毅愛才好士，深相禮接，臨當之郡，遊宴彌日。

translations.literal: Liu Yi loved talent and admired scholars—deeply ritual-greeted—when about to take command—feasted roaming whole days.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi feted him lavishly before posting.

sentences.zh: 行至富陽，慨然歎曰：「看此山川形勢，當復出一伯符。

translations.literal: Traveling reaching Fuyang—sighing deeply said: "Observing this mountain-river terrain—surely another Bo Fu shall emerge.
translations.idiomatic: He prophesied another Sun Ce-style warlord from Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 」何無忌甚慕之。

translations.literal: He Wuji greatly admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji idolized him.

sentences.zh: 東陽，無忌所統，仲文許當便道修謁，無忌故益飲遲之，令府中命文人殷闡、孔寧子之徒撰義構文，以俟其至。

translations.literal: Dongyang—Wuji commanded—Zhongwen promised brief detour paying respects—Wuji deliberately prolonged drinking awaiting—ordered secretarial scholars Yin Chan, Kong Ningzi and cohort compose righteousness-themed essays awaiting his arrival.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji staged literary welcome Zhongwen skipped.

sentences.zh: 仲文失志恍惚，遂不過府。

translations.literal: Zhongwen lost focus distracted—thereupon did not pass mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Distracted Zhongwen bypassed Wuji's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 無忌疑其薄己，大怒，思中傷之。

translations.literal: Wuji suspected slight toward himself—greatly angry—thought to wound him.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji read snub and plotted revenge.

sentences.zh: 時屬慕容超南侵，無忌言于劉裕曰：「桓胤、殷仲文並乃腹心之疾，北虜不足為憂。

translations.literal: At time belonging to Murong Chao southern invasion—Wuji spoke to Liu Yu: "Huan Yin and Yin Zhongwen together constitute gut diseases—northern barbarians not worth worry.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji urged Liu Yu to purge Yin before worrying Later Yan.

sentences.zh: 」義熙三年，又以仲文與駱球等謀反，及其弟南蠻校尉叔文伏誅。

translations.literal: "Yixi third year—again charged Zhongwen with Luo Qiu plotting rebellion—together younger brother Colonel of Southern Man Shuwen executed.
translations.idiomatic: In 407 Liu Yu executed Zhongwen brothers for conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 仲文時照鏡不見其面，數日而遇禍。

translations.literal: Zhongwen at time gazed in mirror—could not see his face—several days then met calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Mirrors stopped reflecting his face—then came arrest.

sentences.zh: 仲文善屬文，為世所重，謝靈運嘗云：「若殷仲文讀書半袁豹，則文才不減班固。

translations.literal: Zhongwen excelled composing texts—esteemed by generation—Xie Lingyun once said: "If Yin Zhongwen read half as much as Yuan Bao—literary talent would not yield to Ban Gu.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Lingyun quipped he read too little.

sentences.zh: 」言其文多而見書少也。

translations.literal: "Meaning his writings abundant yet books seen few.
translations.idiomatic: Much prose, little scholarship.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：桓玄纂凶，父之余基。

translations.literal: Historian says: Huan Xuan seized viciousness—father's leftover foundation.
translations.idiomatic: The historian traces Xuan's villainy to Huan Wen's legacy.

sentences.zh: 挾奸回之本性，含怒於失職；

translations.literal: Embracing treacherous bent—harboring rage at lost posts;
translations.idiomatic: Spite drove him after demotion.

sentences.zh: 苞藏其豕心，抗表以稱冤。

translations.literal: Packaging pig hearts—submitting memorials proclaiming grievance.
translations.idiomatic: He masked ambition with martyr rhetoric.

sentences.zh: 登高以發憤，觀釁而動，竊圖非望。

translations.literal: Climbing high to vent fury—watching cracks to move—secretly plotting undue hopes.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed power on others' crises.

sentences.zh: 始則假寵于仲堪，俄而戮殷以逞欲，遂得據全楚之地，驅勁勇之兵，因晉政之陵遲，乘會稽之酗ＪＴ，縱其狙詐之計，扇其陵暴之心，敢率犬羊，稱兵內侮。

translations.literal: First borrowing favor from Zhongkan—soon slaughtering Yin to indulge desire—thereupon grasping all Chu lands—driving fierce troops—because Jin government declined—riding Kuaiji's drunken turmoil—unleashing deceitful schemes—fanning tyrannical hearts—daring lead dogs and sheep—raising arms insulting within.
translations.idiomatic: He used Zhongkan, murdered Yin, exploited eastern decadence, then marched on Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 天長喪亂，凶力實繁，逾年之間，奄傾晉祚，自謂法堯禪舜，改物君臨，鼎業方隆，卜年惟永。

translations.literal: Heaven lengthened turmoil—vicious strength truly prolific—within a year-span suddenly overturned Jin mandate—self-thinking modeled Yao-Shun abdication—changing creatures facing south—dynastic enterprise just rising—divined years everlasting.
translations.idiomatic: For one shining moment he believed his dynasty eternal.

sentences.zh: 俄而義旗電發，忠勇雷奔，半辰而都邑廓清，逾月而凶渠即戮，更延墜曆，復振頹綱。

translations.literal: Presently loyal banners lightning-struck—faithful warriors thunder-rushed—half-day and capital cleared—past month chief villains executed—extending fallen calendar—reviving ruined norms.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu smashed him within weeks.

sentences.zh: 是知神器不可以暗幹，天祿不可以妄處者也。

translations.literal: This teaches divine regalia cannot be seized in darkness—Heaven's salary cannot be grasped rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Regalia and mandate resist theft.

sentences.zh: 夫帝王者，功高宇內，道濟含靈，龍宮鳳曆表其祥，彤雲玄石呈其瑞，然後光臨大寶，克享鴻名，允彳奚後之心，副樂推之望。

translations.literal: As for emperors—merit towers within cosmos—way saves living beings—dragon palace phoenix calendar displays auspice—crimson clouds dark stones present omens—thereafter radiance assumes great treasure—able to enjoy vast name—matching obedient successor hearts—fulfilling joyful-push expectation.
translations.idiomatic: True sovereigns earn cosmic omens before enthronement.

sentences.zh: 若桓玄之麼麼，豈足數哉！

translations.literal: Like Huan Xuan's insignificance—how worth reckoning!
translations.idiomatic: Petty usurpers scarcely merit mention.

sentences.zh: 適所以幹紀亂常，傾宗絕嗣，肇金行之禍難，成宋氏之驅除者乎！

translations.literal: Just enough to violate norms overturn constants—topple clan cut heirs—open Metal Element's calamity—complete Song house's expulsion!
translations.idiomatic: He only paved Liu Song's rise.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：靈寶隱賊，世載凶德。

translations.literal: Encomium says: Lingbao concealed bandit—generations bore vicious virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Verse brands Lingbao a born rebel.

sentences.zh: 信順未孚，奸回是則。

translations.literal: Trust and obedience not yet secured—treachery became model.
translations.idiomatic: Faith never touched him—guile did.

sentences.zh: 肆逆遷鼎，憑威縱慝。

translations.literal: Wantonly rebel—moving cauldrons—relying on might indulging evil.
translations.idiomatic: He stole thrones by terror.

sentences.zh: 違天虐人，覆宗殄國。

translations.literal: Defying Heaven tormenting people—overturning clan extinguishing state.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and folk abandoned him—clan perished.
